title: Resolving the Sensitivity–Specificity Trade‐Off in Fluorescent Probes via a Tandem‐Activatable Shielding Strategy
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT For precise tumor diagnosis, the intrinsic trade‐off between sensitivity and specificity in fluorescent probes remains a longstanding bottleneck, underscoring an urgent need for strategies to break this fundamental constraint. To address the specificity limitation, we exploited a highly polarity‐sensitive fluorescent scaffold to construct a tandem‐activatable probe, enabling sequential activation by the acidic tumor microenvironment and the angiogenic marker aminopeptidase N. Whereas the single‐locked counterpart is prone to premature activation in circulation, the tandem‐locked probe remains inactive owing to a maleamic acid‐based shielding unit and is activated only upon encountering these two tumor hallmarks. Furthermore, this shielding strategy increases probe hydrophobicity, enhancing tumor uptake and driving accumulation of released fluorophores in low‐polarity lipid droplets, where fluorescence is markedly amplified to improve imaging sensitivity. The probe exhibits rapid and specific activation across various solid tumors with minimal toxicity, thus effectively resolving the sensitivity‐specificity trade‐off in probe design for in vivo applications.

title: Artificial Regulatory T Cells Orchestrate Phase‐Spanning Regeneration in Refractory Tissue Injuries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Regulatory T cells (Tregs) possess potent multiphasic reparative capacity; however, their application is limited by ethical and regulatory challenges associated with live cell therapies. Treg‐derived exosomes (TExo) exhibit low immunogenicity while enriching regenerative signaling relative to parental Tregs. Current exosome carriers place greater emphasis on sustained release than on factors affecting vesicle stability, such as nonspecific interactions and confinement effects. Inspired by the multivesicular body (MVB), we engineered artificial Tregs (ATregs) with an MVB‐like architecture that integrates vesicle protection with sustained release through a reconstructed storage microenvironment. This design enables phase‐aligned TExo release and extends functional activity by more than an order of magnitude compared with free TExo. ATregs sequentially coordinate the suppression of inflammation, enhancement of angiogenesis, and stimulation of skin appendage regeneration. In diabetic wounds and deep second‐degree burn models, which represent intrinsic repair dysfunction and severe structural tissue loss, ATregs markedly accelerate healing and outperform conventional strategies across murine and porcine models. These findings overcome the key limitations of exosome therapies and open a new avenue for next‐generation regenerative therapeutics.

title: Electrochemical Control of Scholl Reaction: Arenium Cation Versus Radical Cation Pathways
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The Scholl reaction is a cornerstone method for constructing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, yet its mechanism remains highly debated because arenium and radical cation intermediates are difficult to characterize. Herein, we demonstrate that electrochemical oxidation provides precise mechanistic control: a low‐potential acidic (LPA) condition selectively favors the arenium cation pathway, whereas a high‐potential neutral (HPN) condition promotes the radical cation pathway. While it is often assumed that only one mechanism operates under a given set of chemical oxidation conditions, our results reveal that most substrates can react via both pathways. Dialkoxyphenyl groups are found to facilitate the radical cation pathway, although no general correlation with overall substrate electron richness is observed. This electrochemical control provides the experimental basis to re‐evaluate previously proposed mechanisms for certain substrates. We demonstrate that switching between LPA and HPN conditions yields different products from the same 3,3’‐diphenyl‐2,2′‐binaphthalene substrate, thereby correcting the computational assignment of the corresponding pathways. Additionally, we show that a tetracene‐derived substrate undergoes cyclodehydrogenation through the arenium cation pathway, revising the computationally assigned dication mechanism for this transformation. Collectively, these results establish electrochemistry as a powerful alternative to traditional chemical oxidation, offering unprecedented experimental control to resolve fundamental mechanistic debates about the Scholl reaction.

title: Stabilizing Functional Nucleic Acids for Real‐Sample Diagnostics
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Functional nucleic acids (FNAs), including aptamers and DNAzymes, offer programmable recognition and catalysis for biosensing, but their performance in real samples is often compromised by nuclease degradation, matrix effects, and interface‐associated losses. For diagnostic translation, stability must, therefore, be defined not only as strand persistence, but as retained folding, binding, catalysis, and signal generation under assay‐relevant conditions. This review examines strategies for stabilizing FNAs in complex biological matrices and organizes the field around four design levers: Chemical, topological, architectural, and microenvironment/interface engineering. Chemical modification of sugars, backbones, and bases can reduce nuclease susceptibility, but requires functional validation. Topological approaches, including terminus shielding, circularization, covalent locking, and mechanically interlocked structures, limit strand accessibility, and reinforce functional conformations. Architectural strategies use multivalency, scaffolded presentation, DNA nanostructures, and rolling circle amplification‐derived concatemers to improve robustness and signal retention. Microenvironment engineering further stabilizes FNAs through controlled immobilization, antifouling interfaces, nanomaterial‐assisted protection, hydrogel or microgel confinement, and sample processing. Case studies in saliva, serum, urine, and stool illustrate how these levers can be combined to enable reliable FNA‐based real‐sample diagnostics.

title: Persistent Mn 3+ Sites on Reduced MnO Enable Efficient Syngas Conversion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Mn‐based materials are widely used for syngas conversion, where MnO is generally regarded as the catalytically active phase under reducing conditions. Yet catalysts derived from different Mn oxide precursors often exhibit markedly different performances despite evolving into the same MnO bulk structure during reaction. Here we show that trace Mn 3+ sites stabilized on oxygen‐deficient MnO surfaces serve as the decisive active sites. Time‐resolved energy‐dispersive x‐ray absorption spectroscopy combined with iterative target transformation factor analysis and depth‐resolved synchrotron photoemission spectroscopy reveals a persistent minor Mn 3 O 4 ‐like spectral contribution and its enrichment near the surface of Mn 2 O 3 ‐derived MnO. These stabilized sites strongly enhance CO adsorption and activation, thereby promoting C─O bond cleavage and markedly improving activity and selectivity for syngas‐to‐light‐olefin conversion. More broadly, this work reveals how minority surface sites can govern catalytic function despite identical bulk phases and establishes an operando strategy for quantitatively resolving low‐coverage active sites in reducible oxide catalysts.

title: NMR Spectroscopic Evidence for Magnetically Induced Ring Currents in All-Metal-Aromatic [Bi4]4+
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Experimental assignment of aromaticity in all-metal systems remains challenging, particularly for heavy-element clusters, where local magnetic effects can obscure signatures of circular electron delocalization. Here, we investigate a supramolecularly stabilized, formally tetracationic [Bi4]4+ ring by combining structurally meaningful reference compounds, solid- and solution-state NMR spectroscopy, SQUID magnetometry, and exact two-component relativistic calculations. Comparison with an isostructural [Li4Br]3+-encapsulated analogue and a binuclear Bi(III) reference compound disentangles global ring-current effects from local heavy-atom deshielding and ligand-specific conformational effects. On this basis, the unusually downfield-shifted 1H and 13C NMR signals observed for the Bi4-containing species provide direct spectroscopic evidence for magnetically induced ring currents in the [Bi4]4+ core. By contrast, bulk magnetic measurements do not reveal significant diamagnetic exaltation, indicating that this quantity is not a resolved descriptor of aromaticity in these systems. Stoichiometric studies further identify chemically competent intermediates that provide mechanistic snapshots of [Bi4]4+ ring formation. Complementary calculations support the assignment of a magnetically responsive, σ-delocalized [Bi4]4+ core, reproduce a rare spectroscopically observed puckering motion of the rhomboidal [Bi4]4+, and underscore the critical role of spin–orbit coupling on electronic structure and dynamics. Overall, this work moves the discussion of aromaticity from predominantly computational assignment toward experimentally benchmarked analysis in the heavy-element and all-metal regime.

title: Circular RNA Delivery In Vitro and In Vivo Using Doubly Branched Aminoethoxy-Functionalized Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Circular RNA is a therapeutically promising RNA modality with superior stability and extended protein expression relative to linear RNA. While delivery systems for linear RNA have received much attention, less effort has been directed toward the delivery of circular RNA, whose closed topology and physicochemical properties differ from those of linear RNAs. Here, we disclose a class of ionizable lipids that enable efficient in vitro and in vivo delivery of circular RNA. These ionizable lipids are step-economically accessible, allowing facile assessment of their structure–delivery relationships. Our studies reveal key elements that enhance circular RNA delivery in vitro and in vivo, including aminoethoxy head units, doubly branched tails and linkers tuned for hydrogen bonding and biodegradability. The lead ionizable lipid for circular RNA delivery, iL-19, incorporating these features, achieves ∼28-fold higher protein expression in C2C12 myocytes than Moderna’s SM-102 formulation and 2.5-fold higher expression upon intramuscular administration in BALB/c mice. iL-19 also surpasses benchmark ionizable lipids ALC-0315 (7.8-fold) and DLin-MC3-DMA (33.4-fold) for intramuscular circular RNA delivery in vivo under otherwise identical conditions. This study establishes design principles and a step-economical synthesis for accessing ionizable lipids that enable highly efficient in vitro and in vivo circular RNA delivery.

title: Metal Fluorides: All-In-One Supports for Ruthenium-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ammonia, an emerging energy carrier, demands advanced catalysts for synthesis under mild conditions to integrate with green hydrogen. We herein establish a family of metal fluoride supports (MFn, M = Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, or Ba) as a tunable “all-in-one” platform for ruthenium (Ru) catalysts. These Ru/MFn systems unify the critical merits of various existing catalysts, such as support-mediated activation of reactants and air stability. Varying the host cation can direct the catalytic pathway. Consequently, Ru/NaF exhibits excellent turnover frequency, while Ru/BaF2 delivers an NH3 synthesis rate of 58.0 mmolNH3 gcat–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 0.9 MPa─surpassing all reported Ru-based catalysts with ≤4 wt % Ru and without external promoters. Advanced characterization reveals that the fluorine vacancy formation energies of the alkali and alkaline-earth lattices, together with the vacancy-reactant interactions, dictate the divergent catalytic mechanisms mediated by different active sites. This work expands the chemistry of metal fluorides, launching a new paradigm for potentially viable NH3-synthesis under mild conditions.

title: Hydrogenation of CO2 to Propane and n -Butane by Engineering Metal Oxide Interfacial Structure and Manipulating Zeolite Pore Structure and Acidity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective hydrogenation of CO2 to propane and n-butane is of great interest, as these two compounds are not only primary components of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) but also crucial raw materials for preparing propene and a degradable plastic precursor of succinic acid. Although various composite catalysts combining metal oxides and zeolites have been explored, their catalytic performances remain insufficient. Here, we found that ZnZrOx decorated with ultrasmall FeOx clusters, forming an intimate FeOx–ZnZrOx interfacial structure, showed high catalytic activity for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol due to a strong CO2 adsorption capacity and H2 dissociation ability, and silicoaluminophosphate molecular sieve with RHO topological structure enhanced methanol conversion into propane and n-butane via hexamethylbenzenes as active hydrocarbon pool species owing to its unique supercage structure and double eight-membered ring pore opening. As a result, coupling of these two materials delivers a CO2 conversion of ∼66% and a (propane + n-butane) selectivity of 82% in hydrocarbons, which leads to a (propane + n-butane) yield of ∼42%. It is surprising that this composite preferentially produces n-butane rather than iso-butane, and the n-butane/iso-butane ratio is higher than 85.8. The high catalytic stability of this composite is demonstrated by maintaining CO2 conversion, (propane + n-butane) selectivity in hydrocarbons, and their yield of ∼ 61%, ∼ 77%, and ∼ 31%, respectively, after a reaction of 620 h. This work not only fabricates a high-performance catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation to propane and n-butane by engineering the metal oxide interfacial structure and manipulating the zeolite’s pore structure and acidity, but also makes it possible to develop an efficient way for preparing propene and succinic acid from CO2 hydrogenation.

title: Electroanalytical and Computational Investigation of Oxoammonium-Mediated Hydride Transfer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer is an important yet relatively underexplored elementary step in C–H functionalization. In this work, we employed cyclic voltammetry (CV) to measure the rates of hydride transfer between electrochemically generated oxoammonium catalysts and 42 substrates including ethers, carbamates, amides, and sulfonamides. Through quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, we uncovered a new transition-state model for hydride transfer in which the N atom of the catalyst resides near a heteroatom (X = N or O) of the substrate to allow alignment of the oxoammonium’s O═N+ motif and the substrate’s forming C═X+ bond. Energy decomposition analysis was subsequently performed to elucidate the key factors that govern the kinetics of oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer. Beyond conventional electronic and steric considerations, we identified substrate distortion, secondary orbital interactions, and noncovalent interactions as critical factors that influence hydride transfer reactivity. We anticipate that these kinetic data along with the mechanistic insights they provide will inform future catalyst development and synthetic applications to broaden the scope of oxoammonium catalysis.

title: Selective Consecutive Decarboxylation Enables Skeletal Contraction of Waste PET
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Direct catalytic upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) to benzene through consecutive decarboxylation contracts the terephthalate-derived C8 framework to C6, representing a skeletal-editing strategy for aromatic polycarboxylates. The key challenge is to control pathway selection across consecutive decarboxylation steps, favoring sequential aryl–carboxyl C–C bond cleavage over competing hydrogenolysis while preserving the aromatic core. Herein, we report an efficient direct catalytic conversion of waste PET to benzene, achieving an exceptionally high yield of 83.3% over a tailored Ru/W0.4ZrOx catalyst. The performance arises from synergistic acid-site reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering. Moderate WOx incorporation into ZrO2 converts Lewis acidity into Brønsted acidity, while oxygen vacancies and WOx species promote adsorption and activation of carboxyl groups. In cooperation with Ru nanoparticles, these features preferentially stabilize the decarboxylation intermediate over its hydrogenolysis counterpart, directing both consecutive steps toward C–C bond cleavage while suppressing undesired hydrogenolysis pathways. Controlled hydrogen supply and a deliberately designed dodecane/water mixed solvent system further enhance selectivity. The catalyst performs effectively across diverse real-world PET wastes, with preliminary techno-economic and life-cycle analyses indicating favorable process-level metrics under the evaluated assumptions. More broadly, these mechanistic insights establish synergistic acidity and oxygen-vacancy regulation as a catalyst-design principle for decarboxylative skeletal editing of aromatic polycarboxylates.

title: Engineering a Reconfigurable Transmembrane Receptor Enables Logic-Controlled Signal Translocation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transmembrane receptors relay extracellular cues into intracellular responses through reconfigurable conformational changes, yet engineering synthetic systems that emulate receptor-like signal translocation with programmable control remains challenging. Here, we engineer a reconfigurable transmembrane receptor that enables logic-controlled signal translocation across lipid membranes. The receptor is constructed from an oriented Y-shaped triplex DNA architecture that inserts directionally into the plasma membrane via dual cholesterol anchors and integrates two environmental inputs─H+ and ATP─through an i-motif and an aptamer module. Under dual-input conditions, cooperative duplex-to-triplex switching triggers reconfigurable structural rearrangement and drives transmembrane relocation of a signaling strand from the outer to the inner membrane leaflet. This receptor-mediated signal translocation converts extracellular chemical cues into spatially defined intracellular activation. The repositioned strand serves as a modular intracellular effector that can be functionalized to implement programmable reactions, including bioorthogonal catalysis and light-triggered photocatalysis at the membrane interface. Importantly, endogenous tumor-microenvironmental cues trigger receptor reconfiguration and signal translocation in 3D tumor spheroids and in vivo, enabling logic-gated intracellular photocatalysis and >85% tumor growth inhibition in xenograft models. By coupling logic-gated reconfigurable switching with directional transmembrane signal propagation, this work establishes an engineered transmembrane receptor for programmable intracellular activation and provides a general strategy for synthetic signal translocation in living systems.

title: Deciphering Interheme Electron-Transfer Pathways in a Diheme Peroxidase from Methane-Oxidizing Bacteria
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bis-FeIV-forming enzymes represent an emerging paradigm in high-valent heme iron chemistry, in which two hemes separated by 15–20 Å are both oxidized to the FeIV state. A tryptophan positioned between the two hemes in two out of the three known enzymes to form this state, MauG and MbnH, has been proposed as the dominant pathway for interheme electron transfer. .The third enzyme, BthA, instead has a serine at this position. Here, we used site-directed mutagenesis of Trp113 in MbnH to test whether this tryptophan is uniquely required for interheme electron transfer. Computational pathway analysis identified the possibility of an alternative, noncovalent route mediated by Arg283 and a heme propionate with possible electronic coupling comparable to that of the native tryptophan pathway. Consistent with this prediction, only simultaneous disruption of both the tryptophan and propionate-mediated pathways abolished bis-FeIV formation entirely. Moreover, only mutants capable of forming bis-FeIV retained the ability to turnover substrate, directly establishing this high-valent state as the catalytic intermediate responsible for substrate modification. These results demonstrate that an intervening tryptophan is not required for fast interheme electron transfer, and instead reveal an additional, noncovalent pathway that may be a general feature of diheme peroxidases.

title: Birch-Type-Reduced Carbazole Anions Enable Redox-Adaptive Super-Reducing Photocatalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds is constrained by the redox potential of the catalyst. Here, we report a redox-adaptive photocatalytic strategy in which an electron-rich carbazole photocatalyst, CBZ6, functions as a molecular redox transformer through the formation of Birch-type carbazole anions. Under visible light, CBZ6 switches between a neutral state for conventional photoredox reactions and an anionic state for super-reducing catalysis. Excitation of the anionic state generates a super-reducing species with an excited-state oxidation potential of approximately −3.6 V versus SCE, substantially beyond that of the neutral excited state (−2.2 V). This adaptive redox switching enables activation of otherwise inaccessible C–F bonds in aryl fluorides, polyfluoroalkyl compounds, and fluoropolymers. The complementary reactivities of the two states further enable diverse photoredox transformations, establishing redox adaptation as a strategy for expanding the accessible reactivity of organic photocatalysts.

title: Cesium-Induced Stabilization of the FeOOH Cocatalyst on Bismuth Vanadate Photoanode for Ultraefficient and Stable Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing active and durable water oxidation cocatalysts is essential for advancing photoelectrochemical (PEC) water-splitting systems. This study investigates the cesium-induced reconstruction of the FeOOH cocatalyst on a bismuth vanadate (BVO) photoanode for the water oxidation reaction, with a focus on the reconstruction process and its effect in improving interfacial charge transfer and photostability. Cesium ions induce the reconstruction of Fe species on the BVO/FeOOH photoanode during the PEC process, leading to the formation of a robust Cs-incorporated FeOOH (Cs:FeOOH) catalytic layer. Spectroscopic analysis combined with open-circuit potential measurement reveals that the in situ formed Cs:FeOOH cocatalyst can effectively protect BVO and promote interfacial hole transfer during PEC operation. As a result, the BVO/Cs:FeOOH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.29 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE and maintains stable operation for over 100 h. Furthermore, the Cs-incorporated FeOOH cocatalyst strategy can be extended to other semiconductor systems, including TiO2 and FeOx, highlighting its broader potential for improving solar-driven PEC water oxidation.

title: Formamidinium-Solvent Intermediates Mediate Self-Seeding Crystallization for Efficient Inverted α-FAPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3) perovskites are promising for high-performance solar cells; however, the low surface energy of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) impedes α-phase nucleation in inverted devices. Here, we report a formamidinium (FA)-solvent intermediate-mediated self-seeding crystallization strategy to enable quality α-phase FAPbI3. By employing N-formylmorpholine (NFM) as a non-toxic solvent, (FA···NFM)PbI3 intermediates are formed, thereby lowering the phase-transition barrier and promoting the spontaneous formation of α-phase nuclei at the early stage of crystallization. These preformed nuclei serve as intrinsic seeds, facilitating rapid nucleation and orientated crystal growth. Consequently, NFM-based devices achieve efficiencies of 26.41% and 26.56% using 2-methoxyethanol (2-Me) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) as primary solvents, respectively, with a 1 cm2 device reaching 25.47%. The unencapsulated devices retain 85% and 90% of their initial efficiencies after 1200 h illumination and 1400 h thermal aging at 85 °C, respectively.

title: Improving the Calendar Life of Silicon Anodes with Inorganic Solid–Electrolyte Interphases
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon anodes unlock higher energy density in Li-ion batteries but suffer from poor calendar life due to inadequately passivating solid–electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Here, we contrast the calendar aging behaviors of single- and mixed-salt locally superconcentrated electrolytes (LSCEs) against carbonate electrolytes. Mixed-salt LSCE cells retained 96% and 44% of precalendar capacity after one month and then after five months, while carbonate electrolyte cells retained 77% and 1%, respectively. The mixed-salt LSCE advantage is tied to the formation of a predominantly inorganic SEI, evidenced by nanoscale Fourier transform infrared spectromicroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and 3D time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry. After 5 months, however, perturbations to SEIs were evident in all cells, accelerating voltage decay and capacity loss by lithium inventory loss associated with SEI growth. These findings suggest that future electrolytes may benefit from strategies that continuously reinforce the SEI through controlled anion and solvent redox in LSCEs.

title: Modular Construction of Cyclic and Linear Quaternary Carbon Centers through Visible‐Light‐Induced Triplet Nitrene Transfer Reaction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐carbon quaternary centers represent a fundamental structural unit found in a wide range of functional molecules. Within the versatile synthetic toolbox, the semipinacol rearrangement (SPR) stands as one of the most powerful tools for assembling this sterically congested motif. In this context, ‌radical‐mediated SPR pathways‌, especially those entailing alkyl migrations, remain underexplored from a strategic standpoint. Herein, we report a visible light‐promoted formal SPR of tertiary allyl alcohols using in situ‐generated triplet nitrene species as the initiator under redox‐neutral conditions. This method demonstrates broad substrate scope, enabling efficient construction of all‐carbon quaternary centers across various steric environments, including rigid cyclic/spiro frameworks and flexible acyclic systems. Mechanistic investigations reveal substrate‐dependent pathways: alkenyl cyclobutanols undergo triplet nitrene addition followed by concurrent ring‐expansion and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to form cyclic ketones, while nonactivated allyl alcohols proceed through aziridination/ring‐opening/SPR sequences to produce linear β‐amino ketones. Preliminary biological assessments of these α‐quaternary β‐aminoketone derivatives revealed that compound 4a exhibited potent anti‐DENV‐2 activity, with an EC 50 value of 0.95 ± 0.02 µM against viral replication.

title: Overcoming the Spin Barrier of Oxygen Redox Chemistry in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries via Metal–Support Magnetic Interaction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT A major bottleneck for the practical application of lithium–oxygen (Li–O 2 ) batteries is the high overpotential resulting from sluggish kinetics of oxygen redox chemistry. This kinetic limitation can rise in part from the spin‐state transition barriers in converting triplet oxygen ( 3 O 2 ) into peroxide species, alongside the parasitic generation of singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ). Here, we demonstrate that metal–support magnetic interactions can effectively overcome this spin barrier. Using palladium (Pd) nanoparticles anchored on ferrimagnetic CoFe 2 O 4 (CFO) substrates as a model catalyst, we reveal that interfacial magnetic coupling restructures the spin and electronic states of Pd sites, generating spin‐polarized active ensembles with optimized adsorption toward oxygen intermediates. This interfacial spin‐electronic effect promotes the conversion of 3 O 2 into peroxide species while suppressing parasitic 1 O 2 evolution during charging, thereby improving the reversibility of oxygen redox chemistry. As a result, the Pd/CFO catalyst achieves a low charging overpotential of 0.05 V and remarkable energy efficiency (91.2%) under spin alignment. This finding establishes metal–support magnetic interaction as a powerful strategy for controlling spin‐dependent oxygen electrocatalysis, providing a general design principle for catalysts involving multi‐site interactions.

title: Regio- and Enantioselective Functionalization of Gaseous Alkanes via Nickel-Catalyzed Alkene Dicarbofunctionalization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The regio- and enantioselective functionalization of gaseous alkanes remains an unsolved challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a general strategy for the asymmetric three-component dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes using readily available gaseous alkanes, including ethane, propane, and isobutane. This transformation, enabled by the merger of hydrogen atom transfer photocatalysis with a chiral nickel catalyst, efficiently delivers chiral α-aryl carbonyl compounds in good yield with excellent regio- and enantioselectivity (up to >20:1 rr and 99:1 er). Experimental and computational studies reveal insights into the mechanism controlling selectivity. Operating under exceptionally mild, energy-efficient conditions, the method unlocks a versatile platform for upgrading feedstock gaseous alkanes into sought-after chiral building blocks.

title: RNA Organelles in DNA‐Based Artificial Cells Provide Spatial Aptamer Functions and Enhanced Signal Processing
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Naturally occurring biomolecular condensates orchestrate key cellular processes by creating spatially distinct reaction environments, yet engineering synthetic condensates that combine structural programmability with spatioselectively encoded function remains challenging. Here, we report multiphase DNA–RNA artificial cells (ACs) that embed functional RNA condensates as organelle‐like compartments within programmable DNA core–shell ACs. A single thermal assembly protocol yields three‐phase ACs comprising a glassy RNA core organelle embedded in a liquid‐like DNA compartment, surrounded by a crosslinked DNA shell. The RNA organelles contain aptamer function, enabling selective protein recruitment and small‐molecule activation, while the DNA scaffold provides independent addressability, modulates RNA‐condensate size, and enhances resistance to serum‐mediated degradation. We further show that RNA chemistry can be used to adjust environmental responsiveness: unmodified RNA organelles undergo rapid degradation in serum and release captured protein cargo, whereas 2′‐fluoro‐modified RNA organelles remain stable for at least 24 h. Finally, by coupling transcriptional modules localized in the DNA core to cell‐free protein translation in the surrounding medium, we establish sender–receiver communication between AC populations and self‐actuating signal processing within individual DNA–RNA ACs. These results establish hybrid nucleic‐acid ACs as programmable, spatially organized systems that couple compartment architecture, RNA molecular recognition, and biochemical communication.

title: Remote‐Controlled Genetic Circuits: Light, Ultrasound, and Magnetic Fields for Programmable Gene Regulation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Remote‐controlled genetic circuits use externally applied physical signals to regulate gene expression and cellular functions with spatial and temporal precision. Light, ultrasound, and magnetic fields provide complementary advantages in controllability, tissue accessibility, and biological compatibility, but their performance depends on both physical‐field propagation and efficient conversion of external energy into intracellular signals and predictable gene‐regulatory outputs. This review presents a unified framework of physical transduction, biological sensors, signal processors, and genetic effectors for comparing prokaryotic and eukaryotic systems. Core genetic circuits are distinguished from delivery and auxiliary platforms that support cargo release, cellular uptake, or energy conversion without directly regulating genes. Representative systems are compared by circuit architecture, transduction mechanism, stimulus parameters, dynamic range, basal leakage, response kinetics, reversibility, in vivo actuation, delivery requirements, and safety. The evolution from inducible switches toward multi‐input logic, tunable regulation, genetic memory, and feedback control is discussed. An end‐to‐end codesign workflow and modality‐specific reporting framework are proposed to integrate physical inputs, transducers, genetic circuits, delivery strategies, and stimulation devices. Quantitative benchmarking and standardized safety evaluation are essential for advancing these systems toward predictable and clinically translatable therapeutic platforms.

title: Neutrophil Extracellular Trap‐Mimetic DNA Nets Enable Concurrent Bacteria‐Targeted Eradication and Toxin Neutralization
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Current antibacterial therapies often suffer from limited bacterial selectivity, host‐cell toxicity, and inflammation triggered by toxin release during bacterial killing. Here, we report a neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)‐mimetic, dopamine‐incorporated DNA net, termed D A Net‐DA, enabling targeted bacterial eradication and concurrent toxin neutralization. Inspired by the trap‐kill‐neutralize function of NETs, D A Net‐DA selectively captures and traps bacteria, followed by in situ catalytic formation of polydopamine nanoshells on the trapped bacteria. This process enables efficient photothermal bacterial eradication while minimizing damage to host cells. Meanwhile, the nanoshells act as molecular sponges to sequester and neutralize bacterial toxins, thereby mitigating toxin‐associated inflammation. These integrated functions endow D A Net‐DA with potent therapeutic efficacy in vivo, as demonstrated by markedly reduced bacterial burdens, toxin levels, tissue inflammation in both conventional and burn wound infection models. Moreover, the simultaneous clearance of bacteria and residual toxins alleviates pro‐inflammatory macrophage polarization, thereby accelerating wound tissue regeneration. This work presents a NETs‐mimetic antibacterial strategy that integrates pathogen clearance with toxin neutralization, offering a promising method for treating bacterial infection‐associated diseases.

title: Vacancy‐Associated La–Ir Pairs Enable Water‐Derived Oxygen‐Hydroxyl Coupling for Durable Low‐Ir PEM Water Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly stable, low‐iridium catalysts is critical for acidic oxygen evolution, but is limited by structural degradation driven by acid corrosion and voltage polarization. Herein, we report an iridium and lanthanum co‐doped manganese‐cobalt spinel catalyst, Ir,La‐MCO δ , featuring octahedral La–Ir pairs (La oct –Ir oct ) with a theoretical favorable configuration of adjacent bridging and Ir z ‐axis oxygen vacancies. This low‐Ir catalyst Ir,La‐MCO δ (0.12 mg Ir cm −2 ) exhibits an overpotential of merely 220 mV at 10 mA cm −2 in pH = 1 electrolyte, and demonstrates robust operation for over 1550 h at 1 A cm −2 in a proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer. Coupled (quasi)in situ characterizations and operando spectroscopy reveal that the adjacent oxygen vacancies mediate the evolution of oxygen intermediates, enabling water‐derived oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling with negligible lattice oxygen involvement, via a decoupled proton–electron transfer pathway. This mechanism preserves the structural integrity of the catalyst and yields a calculated reaction free‐energy change of merely 0.38 eV ( U = 1.23 V) for the most unfavorable oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling elementary step, thereby endowing Ir,La‐MCO δ with exceptional durability. This work provides a valuable mechanistic insight into designing highly stable defective catalysts.

title: Biomaterial‐Based Controlled Release Systems for Spinal Cord Remyelination
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers a complex secondary injury cascade characterized by oligodendrocyte (OL) death and axonal demyelination, leading to permanent neurological deficits. Despite the presence of endogenous oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs), the inhibitory microenvironment—marked by inflammation, glial scarring, and biochemical barriers—prevents effective remyelination. Traditional pharmacological treatments are further hindered by the blood‐spinal cord barrier and rapid clearance of intrathecal injections. This review examines the evolution of controlled release systems engineered to modulate the oligodendroglial lineage. We analyze macro‐ and micro‐scale platforms, including scaffolds, which provide mechanical and topographical cues to direct the fate of OLs and OPCs. Furthermore, we discuss advanced nanoscale vectors, such as nanoparticles and exosomes, designed to deliver high‐value payloads—including small molecules and therapeutic oligonucleotides—directly to the lesion site while minimizing systemic toxicity. Finally, we address critical translational gaps to bridge the divide between preclinical innovation and clinical application in restoring neural connectivity.

title: Fan Hong
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: "My long-term goal is the development of nucleic acid-based molecular systems that allow us to see and interact with biological systems… The most exciting thing about my research is seeing the beauty and complexity of the molecular composition of life…" Find out more about Fan Hong in his Introducing… Profile.

title: Topological Engineering of NIR‐II Emissive Conjugated Oligomers With Unexpected Excited‐State Manifolds for Efficient Phototheranostics and Cancer Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Phototheranostic agents operating in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window hold great potential for precision cancer therapy, yet the rational regulation of excited‐state processes to simultaneously optimize fluorescence and phototherapeutic performances remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report a topology‐driven excited‐state engineering strategy for constructing conjugated oligomers with tailored excited‐state manifolds and multi‐channel excitation dynamics. By precisely manipulating molecular topology, conjugated topological oligomers achieve enhanced light‐harvesting capability and optimized exciton utilization, thereby enabling synergistic regulation of excitation dynamics. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, nanoparticles (NPs) derived from TBT‐3 exhibit 2.8‐fold enhanced NIR‐II fluorescence brightness, 2.7‐fold improved photothermal performance, and 7.5‐fold increased total reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation compared with TBT‐1. In vivo studies demonstrate that TBT‐3 NPs enable high‐resolution NIR‐II fluorescence imaging and efficient tumor elimination. Moreover, TBT‐3‐mediated phototherapy induces immunogenic cell death and enhances antitumor immunity, leading to improved therapeutic efficacy when combined with anti‐PD‐1 immune checkpoint blockade. This work provides a molecular topology‐based strategy for manipulating excited‐state landscapes and establishes conjugated oligomers as versatile candidates for NIR‐II phototheranostics and cancer immunotherapy.

title: Programming Hydrophobic Nanocavity of DNA Frameworks for Ultrastable Fluorescent Imaging
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Fluorescent proteins (FPs) are widely used in biological imaging, yet their limited programmability restricts adaptability for advanced nanoscale applications. Synthetic molecular containers offer designable cavities but struggle to simultaneously achieve large dimensions, biocompatible interfaces, and precise microenvironment control. Here we report DNA framework (DNF) dots, highly programmable fluorescent probes constructed by encapsulating Cy3 within three‐dimensional DNA‐encoded hydrophobic nanocavities. Using amphiphilic tetrahedral DNA frameworks with inward‐oriented alkyl chains, we create well‐defined nanocavities (4.8–8.9 nm) with tunable size, shape, and internal chemistry. Single‐molecule analysis reveals that DNF dots enhance photostability (up to 15‐fold) and total photon output (up to 58‐fold), as compared to single Cy3 tagged on single‐stranded DNA. The exceptional photostability and brightness of DNF dots enable stable binding event frequencies exceeding 7500 frames in DNA‐PAINT super‐resolution imaging. Furthermore, integration into light‐inducible DNA hydrogels yields rewritable information encoding platforms. DNF dots thus establish a versatile platform that combines the environmental shielding of fluorescent proteins with the programmability of synthetic molecular containers, introducing a DNA framework‐encoded microenvironment engineering paradigm for ultrastable fluorescent probes.

title: Controlled Hydrogen Delivery by Single‐Atom Ru Accelerates Electrocatalytic Ammonia Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction to ammonia (NORR) offers a dual opportunity for NO remediation and decentralized NH 3 production, yet its efficiency is often limited by competing pathways and unclear structure–function relationships. Here we introduce a reactant‐shunting strategy that installs a guiding electrocatalytic step via isolated Ru atoms to supply surface‐bound * H species and enforce a Langmuir–Hinshelwood (LH) hydrogenation pathway. Using Ru 1 /Co 3 O 4 as a model catalyst, we show that single Ru sites promote water adsorption and dissociation, forming stable Ru‐H intermediates that thermodynamically and kinetically accelerate the coupling‐hydrogenation steps in NORR. The optimized catalyst delivers an NH 3 yield of 533.49 µmol cm −2 h −1 with a 97.19% faradaic efficiency, surpassing state‐of‐the‐art systems. The reactant‐shunting principle further generalizes across multiple oxide hosts, enhancing NH 3 productivity by up to threefold. These findings establish pathway steering through controlled hydrogen delivery as a powerful strategy for high‐efficiency electrocatalytic ammonia synthesis.

title: Silicate Biomaterials‐Stimulated Vascularized Callus Organoids for Bone Tissue Regeneration
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Organoids that recapitulate native fracture callus can form spontaneous ossification centers within a bone defect, offering substantial promise for rapid bone regeneration. However, existing callus organoids generally lack a functional vascular network and an appropriate mechanical microenvironment, and their production limits scalability and uniformity. Here, we established a droplet‐based microfluidic platform for the high‐throughput generation of morphology‐dependent magnesium silicate‐engineered composite hydrogel microspheres, enabling the uniform construction of vascularized callus organoids. Importantly, morphology‐dependent magnesium silicate could regulate both the bulk mechanical performance and internal stress distribution of the composite hydrogels. In vitro, callus organoids modulated by magnesium silicate nanotubes significantly promoted chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation, developed a stable endothelial network and mineralized structure. Furthermore, magnesium silicate nanotube‐engineered composite hydrogel (2NT‐GM) offered a favorable mechanical microenvironment for callus organoids, thereby activating the mechanotransduction‐related pathway for promoting the development of organoids. In a rat femoral condyle critical‐sized defect model, the vascularized callus organoids regulated by 2NT‐GM were further found to significantly promote vascular network formation, and facilitate bone regeneration at the bone defect center within 6 weeks of implantation. Together, this study suggests a promising strategy for bone tissue regeneration by developing vascularized callus organoids with the stimulation of inorganic silicate biomaterials.

title: In Situ and Operando Techniques for Electrocatalysis in Renewable Energy Applications
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalysis is essential for renewable energy conversion, yet the mechanisms governing catalytic performance remain poorly understood due to the complex nature of electrochemical interfaces. Advances in nanomaterial synthesis and high‐resolution characterization now allow detailed structural and compositional analysis, but static methods fall short of capturing the dynamic behaviors of active sites during operation. In this review, we focus on the growing role of in situ and operando techniques such as optical, X‐ray, and electron‐based, in resolving catalytic structure and reactivity under real‐life working conditions. These methods offer unparalleled access to the evolution of surface species, reaction intermediates, and interfacial topologies that govern catalytic functions. We highlight how in situ and operando studies have revealed transient phenomena and mechanistic details previously inaccessible, and discuss their critical roles in advancing systems for water splitting, CO 2 /N 2 reduction, and fuel cells related renewable energy applications. Beyond highlighting the real‐time transformations captured by operando and in situ methods, this review underscores how coupling operando datasets with theoretical modeling and machine learning can accelerate mechanistic discovery and enable rational catalyst design. By extracting hidden correlations and guiding closed‐loop experimentation, data‐driven approaches promise to reduce reliance on empirical trial‐and‐error and unlock predictive control over catalytic performance. Taken together, these developments position operando characterization, when coupled with AI‐driven interpretation, as a cornerstone of future energy research, providing a pathway to accelerate discovery, design, and deployment of next‐generation electrocatalysts.

title: Biomarker and Bioorthogonality Dual‐Locked Chemiluminescent Probes for Cancer Urine Test
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Bioorthogonality‐activatable optical imaging activates caged or quenched probes via bioorthogonal reactions for disease diagnosis. Although chemiluminescence enables low‐background detection, it has rarely been applied to bioorthogonality‐activatable imaging. Here, we synthesize chemiluminescent tetrazine probes (CLTZs) by coupling a tetrazine acceptor to a phenoxy‐1,2‐dioxetane donor through π‐conjugated vinylene linkers, enabling biomarker and bioorthogonality dual‐locked activation for cancer urine testing. Unlike conventional chemiluminophores, tetrazine in CLTZs mediates an internal‐conversion‐to‐a‐dark‐state quenching mechanism, suppressing chemiluminescence even after phenolate formation. Strong chemiluminescence is restored only when the phenolate form undergoes bioorthogonal reaction with bicyclononyne (BCN), generating pyridazine‐containing donor–π–acceptor chemiluminophores. This unique dark state enables development of an H 2 O 2 and bioorthogonality dual‐locked probe ( H BCP), emitting only when both H 2 O 2 and BCN are present. By engineering BCN into a cancer‐activatable bioorthogonal urinary reporter ( C BUR) that releases renal‐clearable BCN in tumors, a chemiluminescent bioorthogonal pair ( H BCP & C BUR) is created. This pair achieves in vivo tumor imaging with a signal‐to‐background ratio of 438 and detects lung metastasis in early urinary assays with up to 23.9‐fold signal enhancement over healthy mice. This work provides a molecular design for bioorthogonality‐activatable chemiluminescence toward noninvasive, sensitive disease diagnosis.

title: Structural Softness–Rigidity Mediation Enables Multicolor Emission and Long‐Lived Phosphorescence in Hf/Zr Halides
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Multicolor fluorescence, typically favored by soft environments, and phosphorescence, which relies on rigid lattices to stabilize triplet excitons, are fundamentally incompatible and hard to coexist within a single material. Here, we report a crown–ether–directed lattice assembly that integrates [HfCl 6 ] 2‒ /[ZrCl 6 ] 2‒ octahedra and DB18C6@M(K + /Rb + ) supramolecular, yielding four unknown organic–inorganic hybrid Hf/Zr halides. Notably, (DB18C6@K) 2 (CH 3 CN) 2 HfCl 6 achieves an exceptional room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) quantum yield (Φ p ) of 54.43%, a long lifetime of 0.8 s, and a visually discernible afterglow persisting up to 6 s. Moreover, these materials exhibit excitation–dependent multicolor emission, producing green and blue–white outputs under 302 and 365 nm irradiation, respectively. This unique multimodal luminescence originates from the synergistic interplay between the balanced soft‐rigid lattice provided by the crown‐ether framework and heavy – atom Hf/Zr centers, which facilitates intersystem crossing, enabling both efficient RTP and tunable multichannel pathways. It has been confirmed by the high–pressure synchrotron angle–dispersive x–ray diffraction and Raman results. Overall, this work establishes a heavy–atom–based structural mediation which may offer a generalizable route to high‐efficiency, multichannel, and stimuli‐responsive RTP materials.

title: Red Light‐Gated Charge Transfer Enables Trace Oxygen Response in Dye‐Sensitized TiO 2 –Carbon Nanotube Hybrids
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Light offers a powerful means of activating materials with spatial and temporal precision. However, translating excited‐state processes into chemically responsive electronic function in conductive solids remains challenging, particularly under low‐energy red illumination. Herein, we report red light‐gated charge transfer in dye‐sensitized single‐walled carbon nanotube–TiO 2 (SWCNT–TiO 2 ) hybrids that enables trace oxygen detection. Immobilization of red‐absorbing squaraine sensitizers on TiO 2 domains embedded within a conductive SWCNT network reversibly generates a photostationary charge‐transfer state under 628 nm excitation. Despite the low photon energy of red light, the hybrid architecture supports interfacial electron injection into TiO 2 and hole accumulation in the nanotube scaffold, while remaining electronically dormant in the dark. Interception of photogenerated electrons by O 2 perturbs this light‐induced state and converts excited‐state redox chemistry into a chemiresistive signal with ppb‐level sensitivity. This capability enables continuous monitoring of oxygen depletion in a sealed headspace during food spoilage. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, energy‐level alignment analysis, and charge‐carrier inversion experiments show that O 2 triggers light‐activated changes in SWCNT carrier density. These findings demonstrate that low‐energy optical excitation can gate chemical response in dye‐sensitized SWCNT–TiO 2 hybrids, establishing a design strategy for temporally controlled sensing and photoresponsive electronic function.

title: Double Reduction of Ph 3 B to a Dianionic Borane With a Powerful Sr I Intermediate
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Reduction of [(BDI)SrI] 2 with KC 8 generated in situ a (BDI)Sr I species which enabled the reduction of Ph 3 B to the Ph 3 B 2− dianion (BDI = HC[(Me)C═N‐DIPeP] 2 , DIPeP = 2,6‐(Et 2 CH) 2 ‐phenyl). The product (BDI)Sr(BPh 3 )Sr(BDI) features a Ph 3 B 2− dianion that is bridging two Sr 2+ cations by interaction with one of the Ph rings. This polarizes a large part of the electron density in the bridging Ph ring (NPA charge: −1.53) whereas the B is slightly positive (+0.44). The HOMO of the complex mainly consists of the π*‐orbital in the bridging Ph ring overlapping with Sr d ‐orbitals. However, there is also 18% contribution of the B p ‐orbital. In solution, there is coalescence of 1 H NMR signals of all three Ph rings. Complex (BDI)Sr(BPh 3 )Sr(BDI) can react as a 2 e transfer reagent or as a B‐nucleophile. It reacts with I 2 to Ph 3 B and [(BDI)SrI] 2 . Reaction with Ph 3 B led to formation of a Gomberg‐type dimer. The reaction with PhI is smooth and selectively gave (BDI)Sr(Ph 4 B) and [(BDI)SrI] 2 , likely through direct nucleophilic attack of an electron rich B atom at PhI. Isolation of a complex with the elusive Ph 3 B 2− dianion demonstrates the very high reducing power of in situ generated (BDI)Sr I species.

title: Cooperative Agostic‐Type C─H···Cu, Quadrupolar Cu···CO 2 , and C─H···O/π Interactions in an Ultra‐Microporous MOF Enable One‐Step Methane Purification From Quaternary C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 /CH 4
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT While agostic‐type C─H···metal σ‐interactions are central to organometallic catalysis, their role in gas separation remains elusive. In this study, a robust phosphine‐functionalized ultra‐microporous Cu(I/II)‐organic framework, LIFM‐XYY‐15, featuring open metal sites (OMSs) and rich aromatic pore walls, is designed to enable one‐step CH 4 purification from a quaternary C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 /CH 4 mixture. Notably, LIFM‐XYY‐15 exhibits much higher C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 uptakes than CH 4 , showing C 3 H 8 /CH 4 , C 2 H 6 /CH 4 , and CO 2 /CH 4 uptake ratios of 2.46, 2.30, and 3.92 at 298 K and 1 bar, respectively, which are significantly raised to 12.18, 8.59, and 9.89 at 0.1 bar. The separation potentials (∆ q ) reach 22.12 (C 3 H 8 /CH 4 ), 20.34 (C 2 H 6 /CH 4 ), and 43.69 (CO 2 /CH 4 ) cm 3 cm −3 at 298 K and 1 bar, demonstrating excellent CH 4 purification ability from the quaternary mixture. Breakthrough experiments confirm the delivery of high‐purity CH 4 (≥99.9%) with a productivity of 1.39 mol L −1 with excellent recyclability. The in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD), in situ FT‐IR spectroscopy, and molecular simulations reveal that the exceptional selectivity arises from the synergistic interplay of agostic‐type C─H···Cu, quadrupole‐electrostatic Cu···‐CO 2 , and alkane C─H···O/π interactions, which collectively reinforce the affinity for C 2 –C 3 hydrocarbons and CO 2 while disfavoring CH 4 . This work discloses a crucial role of agostic‐type interactions as a powerful yet underexplored design principle for selective hydrocarbon separations.

title: V─O─Ti Bridge‐Bond Polarity Boosts Na + Migration in V‐Based Fluorophosphates for Fast Sodium Storage
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Vanadium‐based fluorophosphates are promising high‐energy‐density cathodes for next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, the pronounced degradation of Na + diffusion at high voltage hinders their fast‐charging capability. Herein, a Ti 4+ ‐doping‐induced bridge‐bond‐polarity‐driven strategy is proposed to reshape the V electronic structure for facilitating V─O electron exchange. Correspondingly, voltage hysteresis, polarization, and structural distortion at high voltage are suppressed, accompanied by enhanced electronic conductivity. Meanwhile, the polar V─O─Ti bridge bonds expand the dominant one‐ and two‐dimensional Na + transport channels by inducing bridging‐O displacement, further boosting Na + migration capability. Therefore, Na 3 V 1.92 Ti 0.08 O(PO 4 ) 2 F 2 with V─O─Ti delivers high capacities of 121.8 and 62.1 mA h g −1 at 0.1C and 50C, respectively, while maintaining excellent cycling stability. Additionally, the 0.92‐Ah Na 3 V 1.92 Ti 0.08 O(PO 4 ) 2 F 2 //HC pouch cell exhibits 80% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 1C. At the 9 Ah scale, the pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 154 Wh kg −1 . This synergistic reinforcement strategy driven by bridge‐bond polarity paves the way for sustainable high‐power polyanionic SIBs.

title: Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe48Mn32Co10Cr10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation.

title: Who leads the global gas market? Geopolitics and price transmission between the U.S. and Europe
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy

title: Self-regenerating photocatalytic water treatment systems: integrating cognitive AI control, bio-inspired self-healing, and thermoelectric energy harvesting
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Conventional photocatalytic water treatment systems face persistent limitations in terms of catalyst deactivation, energy consumption, and adaptability to variable influent quality. This review examines the integration of three emerging technological domains, machine learning driven process optimization, bio-inspired self-healing material strategies, and thermoelectric energy recovery, as a framework for developing more autonomous and resource-efficient photocatalytic treatment systems. A systematic literature search was conducted in Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed (January 2001 to June 2024), following PRISMA guidelines. After multi-step screening, 104 peer-reviewed studies were included in the quantitative synthesis. Reviewed studies reported degradation efficiencies above 85% for model recalcitrant pollutants under optimized conditions. ML approaches, particularly artificial neural networks and ensemble methods, improved predictive accuracy of degradation kinetics by 20–35% relative to empirical models. Self-healing polymeric matrices retained catalytic activity exceeding 80% after repeated use cycles. Thermoelectric modules integrated in solar-driven reactors generated partial energy offsets under laboratory conditions, though full energy self-sufficiency has not yet been demonstrated at the pilot scale. Critical challenges remain, including long-term material stability under real wastewater conditions, scalability of digital twin architectures, and rigorous techno-economic validation. A research roadmap to address these barriers is proposed, with an emphasis on pilot-scale demonstration and standardized performance benchmarking.

title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dynamic remodeling of immune cell-surface glycans reflects cellular state and immune activity. Despite advances in single-cell glyco-profiling, current methods primarily capture pre-existing glycan epitopes, providing limited information on dynamic sialoglycans. Here, we present GlycoStamp-seq, a method to profile nascent sialoglycan dynamics by coupling Ac₄ManNAz-based metabolic glycoengineering with single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) and scDyna-seq. We apply GlycoStamp-seq by injecting Ac₄ManNAz into oxaliplatin-treated mice with subcutaneous bladder tumors, days before extracting tumor-derived single-cell suspensions for sequencing. Following oxaliplatin treatment, a subset of CD8⁺ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment exhibits elevated nascent sialoglycan activity, enhanced effector programs, and increased clonal expansion. Furthermore, elevated nascent sialoglycan levels mark antigen-reactive CD8⁺ T cells with increased anti-tumor efficacy in vitro and in vivo. GlycoStamp-seq may thus serve as a versatile platform for profiling nascent sialoglycan dynamics in complex tissues, thereby expanding the single-cell multi-omics toolkit and providing insights into sialoglycan dynamics during therapeutic response.

title: A probability-box framework for quantifying office building air conditioning flexibility under multi-source uncertainty
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Air conditioning systems are important flexible resources in buildings. However, their flexibility potential is highly uncertain due to unpredictable load disturbances caused by weather and occupancy variations. These uncertainties often lead to inconsistent load reduction outcomes, even when identical operating strategies are applied. To address the challenge of accurate quantification, this study proposes a probability box (P-box) model to characterize such potential under uncertainty. After defining the perturbation ranges and probability distributions of uncertain parameters, a stochastic load scenario generation method is employed, combining Monte Carlo sampling with Savitzky-Golay filtering to simulate multi-source disturbance conditions. The proposed P-box model is then evaluated for its prediction accuracy and adaptability based on these scenarios. The method is demonstrated using a calibrated office-building model in Tianjin under summer cooling conditions. Results show that under temperature reset and precooling strategies, the P-box model yields remarkably low prediction errors, the Wasserstein-based prediction achieves relative errors of 9.22% and 4.58% with respect to load reduction simulated under field-measured inputs, compared with 16.98% and 7.90% for the traditional deterministic methods. Moreover, the 100% P-box interval enveloped all evaluated samples, while narrower confidence intervals provided risk-dependent coverage, which accurately delineates the adjustable load range of buildings under multi-source disturbance conditions. This provides a reliable representation method for flexible resource scheduling and demand response strategy formulation.

title: Dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Unlike passenger electric vehicles, heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles operate for long periods under high-load conditions. The continuous heat rejection of the engine-generator set through the engine high-temperature coolant loop makes fan/pump power directly interact with the direct-current (DC) bus power balance and generator–battery power split. Therefore, cooling power scheduling is part of energy management, rather than only a thermal-protection task. This paper proposes a dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination strategy, termed DTP-HETC, for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles. A shared-encoder dual-head bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) predictor is used to capture short-horizon traction fluctuations and long-horizon engine-loop thermal evolution. The predicted thermal risk is quantified as thermal debt and converted into thermal buffer intensity B T k , which further adapts the thermal-load-shaping weights and the control-grid resolution of dynamic programming-based model predictive control (DP-MPC). By using this information, DTP-HETC advances part of the cooling effort from boundary-triggered response to thermal-risk formation intervals, smoothing cooling-induced DC-bus disturbances and coordinating fan/pump power with generator–battery power allocation. Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 220-ton series hybrid mining truck show that, under sustained heavy-load uphill operation, DTP-HETC reduces equivalent fuel consumption by 12.16% and lowers peak engine-loop coolant temperature by 2.53 °C compared with a rule-based baseline. The mean execution time is 33.7 ms, confirming controller-level real-time feasibility. These results indicate that DTP-HETC provides an effective thermal-load reshaping approach for improving energy efficiency and thermal reliability in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles.

title: Bridging deterministic and stochastic scheduling: Learning risk-aware forecast adjustments for PV-BESS operation
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The participation of hybrid photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) installations in electricity markets requires modeling multi-temporal forecast uncertainty via temporal trajectories and integrating this information into bidding optimization frameworks. Most state-of-the-art approaches rely on stochastic or robust optimization methods, which are computationally intensive and offer limited interpretability to decision-makers. Consequently, deterministic optimization approaches remain the industry standard in practical market applications. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a novel learning-to-optimize framework that combines a deterministic mixed-integer linear programming formulation with a context-aware artificial neural network policy trained through reinforcement learning. The policy operates as a learned cost function approximation , translating probabilistic forecast metrics into time-dependent multiplicative forecast adjustment parameters. This approach preserves the simplicity and industry acceptance of deterministic optimization while effectively embedding information related to forecast uncertainty and risk-awareness into the day-ahead bidding and scheduling process for hybrid PV-BESS systems. For a real-world electric vehicle charging station case study in Portugal, equipped with 375 kWp of PV generation and a 1.258 MWh BESS, the proposed learning-to-optimize framework substantially outperforms the deterministic baseline. Specifically, it captures 39.27% and 27.26% of the maximum theoretical cost-saving potential achievable under perfect forecasts during autumn and summer peak periods, respectively. At the intraday level, the learned policy effectively mitigates systematic forecast errors, reducing the cumulative daily negative imbalance volume by 48.22% under standard operating conditions. Moreover, the framework maintains a robust operational safety margin, reducing imbalance exposure by 10.02% during large unforeseen PV generation drops caused by clouds.

title: Theory-guided lightweight decomposition for efficient and robust day-ahead electrical load forecasting
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Accurate electrical load forecasting is important for operational planning and dispatch in modern power systems, yet existing models often face a trade-off among predictive accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to imperfect exogenous inputs. To address this challenge, we propose a Theory-guided Lightweight Efficient Decomposition (TgLED) framework with a Structured Temporal–Exogenous Mixer (STEM) for day-ahead electrical load forecasting. TgLED transforms raw load data into a normalized load-ratio series and decomposes it into a transferable dimensionless trend and a local fluctuation component. The trend captures stable structural patterns through domain knowledge, whereas the fluctuation is learned by STEM, a lightweight dual-path architecture that separately models temporal inertia and exogenous drivers using efficient feedforward operations. Four-fold cross-validation on hourly load and weather data from 12 districts in Beijing shows that TgLED achieves an average MSE of 0.056, reducing the error by 9.8% compared with the previous theory-guided baseline TgDLF. Compared with recently proposed lightweight time-series forecasting baselines, TgLED achieves evident superiority in forecasting performance. On the same RTX 4090 platform, TgLED reduces the training time from 768.66 s to 6.85 s and the inference time from 19.25 s to 1.91 s, indicating its practical value for frequent retraining and multi-district day-ahead forecasting. Additional noise-injection experiments on weather inputs show slower performance degradation, indicating stronger robustness to exogenous-input uncertainty and weather forecast errors. These results demonstrate that TgLED provides an efficient and interpretable approach to electrical load forecasting under limited computational budgets and imperfect exogenous information.

title: Variational Bayes-based multiple neural network method for battery SOC estimation
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Accurate estimation of battery state of charge (SOC) under complex and varying operating conditions remains challenging. This paper proposes a variational Bayes-based multiple neural network (VBMNN) method for battery SOC estimation. Within the proposed algorithm, a hierarchical probabilistic model based on Dirichlet and categorical distributions is constructed to characterize the model indicator vector and model probability vector. Variational Bayesian inference is employed to obtain approximate posterior distributions of the state, model indicator, and model probability vector. The posterior expectation of the model indicator serves as the fusion weight to combine the information provided by different models, thereby forming a single state posterior distribution. Through a pseudo-measurement formulation, neural networks trained under different operating conditions are incorporated into recursive state estimation as measurement models. In addition, a Student’s t noise model with a latent Gamma variable is introduced to mitigate the effects of outliers and non-Gaussian measurement noise. Experimental results obtained from the tested battery show that VBMNN achieves root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 0.40%, 0.49%, and 0.49% under three driving cycles not used for training. After artificial non-Gaussian noise is introduced, the corresponding RMSEs remain below 0.60%, demonstrating the robustness of the proposed algorithm. Additional tests at different temperatures and cross-cell validation further demonstrate its adaptability to operating conditions not encountered during training and to cell-to-cell variations.

title: A methodology for long-term hourly electricity demand forecasting driven by GDP and invariant load profiles
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Long-term electricity demand forecasting is necessary for grid and operations planning, as well as for the analysis and planning of energy transition strategies. However, accurate long-term load forecasting with high temporal resolution remains a challenge as most existing approaches focus on aggregated forecasts, which require accurate prediction of many other variables. This study proposes a parsimonious methodology that uses t-tests to verify the temporal invariance of historical load profiles and the correlation of load with gross domestic product (GDP) to arrive at a long-term hourly load forecast. Applying this methodology first to a controlled benchmark analysing Singapore’s isolated grid, and of multi-year historical data (2004–2022) reveals that its relative hourly load has remained statistically invariant, with an overall percentage deviation of 4.24% across seasonality indices. Utilizing these invariant historical load profiles, five-year-ahead total yearly forecasts were generated using GDP as a predictor, and the hourly loads were then forecasted using hourly seasonality index fractions. The maximum Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) across multiple experiments of six years ahead forecasts was only 6.87%. To systematically evaluate the generalizability and macroeconomic limitations of this top-down methodology beyond Singapore, the methodology was subsequently tested across six European countries. Results show that the methodology achieves high accuracy (MAPE < 8%) for economies with strong GDP-load correlations (Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Spain) but exhibits some performance degradation in decoupled economies where macroeconomic growth no longer drives electricity demand expansion linearly (Germany, UK). Additionally, invariant seasonality metrics were incorporated into a short-term forecasting model based on exponential smoothing (ES), demonstrating comparable or improved accuracy relative to existing machine learning-based methods. The findings show that parsimonious approaches can be effective in arriving at long-term, high resolution forecasts.

title: Transport characteristics and formation mechanism of voltage inconsistency in 200-cell PEMFC stack: Numerical reconstruction and experimental investigation
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Due to the difficulty in directly observing and resolving internal mass transport in multi-cell proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stacks, current studies on stack voltage inconsistency remain largely confined to macroscopic performance analysis. Consequently, the mechanisms responsible for voltage inconsistency remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, this study develops a framework integrating offline pressure testing, pressure boundary extraction, and grouped numerical reconstruction to investigate internal transport processes and clarify the formation mechanism of voltage inconsistency in large-scale multi-cell stacks. In this framework, pressure data measured at different stack positions are used as boundary conditions to reconstruct the transport behavior of representative cells and analyze stack mass transport characteristics. The reconstructed results are then combined with sensitivity analysis of the experimental data to identify the dominant factors governing stack voltage nonuniformity. Finally, numerical simulations are performed to reproduce the development of low-voltage cells and further verify the proposed mechanism. The results show that the maximum oxygen concentration difference among cells at different stack positions is only 0.4 mol/m 3 , indicating that oxygen distribution differences alone are insufficient to cause significant performance variations. Correlation analysis further indicates that liquid water accumulation at the bottom of the stack is the dominant factor responsible for voltage reduction in the bottom cells. Water-rich simulations demonstrate that increased liquid-water loading in the bottom cells can obstruct oxygen transport and cause voltage decay. This study provides an effective numerical reconstruction method for resolving internal transport processes in multi-cell PEMFC stacks and offers guidance for improving stack cell-voltage consistency.

title: Transport-interface coupling regulates calendar aging in lithium metal batteries
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are promising next-generation energy storage systems, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by rapid capacity loss during long-term storage, known as calendar aging. This degradation is commonly attributed to the chemical instability of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), while the role of electrolyte transport remains largely overlooked. Here, using a model Cl − /NO 3 − -containing electrolyte system with systematically varied glyme chain length (G2-G4), we demonstrate that both SEI chemistry and electrolyte transport properties synergistically influence interfacial stability under static conditions. Shorter glyme chains promote the formation of an SEI enriched in Li 2 O and LiF, whereas longer chains yield a less protective SEI. Meanwhile, increasing solvent chain length progressively deteriorates ionic transport and interfacial kinetics. These combined effects lead to heterogeneous lithium (Li) deposition and porous interfacial structures in electrolytes with longer glyme chains. Under static storage, the less protective SEI together with transport-limited interfacial heterogeneity synergistically accelerates micro-galvanic corrosion, Li loss, and calendar capacity decay, while the SEI with higher Li 2 O/LiF content and favorable transport properties effectively suppresses corrosion. By quantitatively correlating electrolyte transport properties, SEI composition, deposition morphology, corrosion kinetics, and full-cell performance, this work establishes that both the chemical nature of the SEI and the transport capability of the electrolyte are critical design parameters for achieving stable cycling and extended calendar life in LMBs.
