title: Mitochondria–Nanozyme Hybrid Therapeutic for Modulation of the Inflammatory Cascade in Psoriasis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The chronic recurrence of psoriasis is driven by a self-amplifying inflammatory cascade in which oxidative stress and mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction reinforce each other, and single-target conventional therapies often fail to break this cycle. Here, we present a micro–nano hybrid system, Mito-Ce, constructed by covalently immobilizing ceria nanozymes (CeNPs) onto the surface of isolated functional mitochondria through thiol–maleimide chemistry. This design endows the hybrid with dual functionalities, including mitochondrial bioactivity and durable ROS-scavenging capabilities of CeNPs. In H2O2-stimulated macrophages, upon internalization. Mito-Ce markedly reduced intracellular ROS and consequently suppressed the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β). Topical application of Mito-Ce to an imiquimod-induced mouse model of psoriasis visibly resolved psoriatic plaques, reduced the PASI score, and reversed epidermal hyperplasia. Beyond local repair, Mito-Ce rebalanced systemic immunity, evidenced by a decline in splenic pathogenic Th17 cells and polarization toward anti-inflammatory M2 macrophages. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed that Mito-Ce broadly reversed the pathological gene expression program, downregulating stress-responsive and phagocytosis-related genes while upregulating genes associated with metabolism, epidermal proliferation, and tissue homeostatic remodeling. These coordinated networks ultimately re-established immune–barrier homeostasis at the molecular level. Collectively, by integrating nanozyme-mediated ROS scavenging with mitochondrial bioactivity, the Mito-Ce hybrid could treat psoriasis through coordinated disruption of the inflammatory cascade, potentially offering a highly effective platform for various chronic inflammatory disorders.

title: Solvent-Dipole Deshielding of Hydrated Aluminum Lewis Acids for Enhanced 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Production from Biomass
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key biomass-derived platform chemical for producing furan-based fuels, fine chemicals, and polymers. Its production from glucose in homogeneous catalytic systems, however, is often limited by the solvation of Lewis acid catalytic centers, where coordinating solvent molecules and anions can shield the active sites, restrict substrate access, and diminish HMF yield and selectivity. Here, we demonstrate that polar aprotic cosolvents can function as active components of the catalytic microenvironment rather than passive reaction media. In water-rich AlCl3 solutions, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), N,N-dimethylacetamide (DMA), and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) exert dipole–dipole interactions with Al-coordinated water molecules through hydrogen bonding, distorting the [Al(H2O)6]3+ solvation shell and increasing access to the Lewis acidic Al center without directly coordinating to it. Spectroscopic measurements and electronic-structure calculations reveal that weakening of the Al–O(water) interaction increases in the order of DMF < DMA < DMSO. This solvation-shell deshielding decreases the apparent activation energy for glucose-to-fructose isomerization from 96 to 79 kJ·mol–1 and enables an HMF yield of 90% from glucose at 150 °C. Glucose streams derived from sugarcane bagasse, poplar sawdust, and palm trunk sawdust afford HMF yields exceeding 80%, while the integrated sugarcane-bagasse route achieves a 49 mol % HMF yield based on the cellulose originally present in the biomass. These results establish dipolar cosolvent control of hydrated metal centers as a molecular design principle for homogeneous biomass conversion.

title: Nanostructured Quercetin-Lipid Carrier on 3D Printed Scaffolds for Improved Bone Regeneration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Musculoskeletal defects remain difficult to treat because current grafts often have limited supply, donor-site morbidity, risk of immune reaction, or insufficient local biological stimulation. To address this problem, this study developed 3D-printed β-tricalcium phosphate (TCP) scaffolds loaded with quercetin-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers (Que-NLCs) to combine an osteoconductive ceramic structure with local delivery of a natural osteogenic and anti-resorptive compound. Que-NLCs provided controlled release for up to 21 days and reduced the initial burst release compared with free Que at both pH 5.0 and 7.4. At pH 5.0, release was ∼40% for Que and ∼33% for Que-NLCs, while at pH 7.4, release was ∼32% for Que and ∼26% for Que-NLCs. In vitro studies showed that Que-NLC-loaded scaffolds increased osteoblast viability by ∼28.6%, increased alkaline phosphatase activity by 33% by day 11, and reduced osteoclastic activity by 56% by day 21. RT-qPCR further showed up to 4-fold increases in osteogenic markers and up to 60% reduction in osteoclastogenesis-related genes. In a 6-week rat distal femur model, Que-NLC scaffolds increased new bone formation by ∼1.9-fold compared with TCP. These results show that Que-NLC-TCP scaffolds provide a localized, controlled drug-delivery platform to improve bone regeneration in non-load-bearing defects.

title: Interface-Programmed Growth of High-Aspect-Ratio 1D Ni–MOF Nanofibers on MXene for Wearable Enzyme-Free Glucose Sensing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Noninvasive wearable glucose sensors capable of real-time sweat analysis offer a less discomforting alternative for long-term monitoring in patients with diabetes. However, practical implementation remains challenging. Major barriers include insufficient catalytic sensitivity to quantify the low glucose levels in sweat, limited compatibility between nanomaterial synthesis and scalable manufacturing processes, and the lack of a biofluid microenvironment suitable for enzyme-free electrochemical sensing. Here, we address these challenges by combining strong interfacial anchoring on a conductive template with surfactant-assisted growth control to engineer high-aspect-ratio (∼100) 1D Ni–TCPP MOF nanofibers as an active shell on MXene–NH2. In contrast to conventional electrospinning-assisted approaches, the resulting 1D MOF shell is polymer-template-free and thus avoids insulating scaffold components. The resulting fluffy, self-supporting Ni-MOF@MXene architecture is inherently compatible with printed electronics, enabling large-area fabrication of wearable enzyme-free glucose-sensing patches. To overcome the constraints of enzyme-free sensing in physiological biofluids, we further develop an integrated system that combines microfluidics with a NaOH/Nafion/PVA alkaline sustained-release membrane, establishing a localized alkaline microenvironment within sweat to enable continuous analysis.

title: Dry Mask Transfer Lithography for High-Resolution Patterning of Nanomaterials and Molecular Interfaces on Arbitrary Substrates
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract This study introduces dry mask transfer lithography as a versatile microfabrication strategy that integrates the patterning resolution of photolithography with the substrate adaptability of soft lithography. In this method, a photoresist mask is first patterned on an elastomeric polymer stamp and subsequently transferred onto a target substrate by thermally modulating interfacial adhesion and viscoelastic energy dissipation. The process enables high-fidelity pattern formation across a wide range of surfaces including semiconductors, metals, and insulators and even on a curved surface while preventing direct exposure of the target substrate and functional materials to solution-based lithographic chemicals. Utilizing the transferred photoresist pattern as a lift-off mask, the method further enabled patterning of zero-, one-, and two-dimensional colloidal nanomaterials as well as self-assembled molecular layers. Compared with the conventional shadow masking method, the transferred masks provided approximately 6-fold higher pattern precision, with a minimum pattern-edge curvature radius of approximately 0.75 μm. Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopic analysis confirmed that the intrinsic properties of the patterned nanomaterials were preserved. As a functional demonstration, biphilic surfaces fabricated by the method showed a more than 3-fold increase in fog-harvesting efficiency compared with uniform hydrophobic surfaces owing to controlled droplet nucleation, growth, and coalescence. These findings establish dry mask transfer lithography as a broadly applicable platform for high-precision integration of chemically sensitive colloidal nanomaterials onto diverse substrates, offering strong potential for the fabrication of high-performance functional interfaces, nanodevices, displays, and energy-related systems.

title: Thermal Stability of Nitrogen-Doped Tunnel Oxide Passivating Contact Structures for Future Chalcogenide/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chalcogenide/silicon monolithic tandem solar cells (SCs) are regarded as promising candidates for next-generation photovoltaic technology. Tunnel oxide passivating contact (TOPCon) technology, with its inherent resilience to high thermal budgets, is well-suited for the bottom cell in such tandems. To further mitigate parasitic light absorption and carrier nonradiative recombination losses in TOPCon when integrated into tandem devices, a wide-bandgap, nitrogen (N)-doped TOPCon structure is adopted in this work. We investigate its thermal stability after a high-temperature preparation process followed by post-annealing (300–600 °C, 10–30 min) on standalone TOPCon samples. The results indicate that Si–Hn bonds in the N-doped TOPCon structure are more prone to breakage during high-temperature processing than those in N-free counterparts, revealing fragile thermal stability. During post-annealing, substantial hydrogen released from the SiNx:H dielectric layer recombines with Si dangling bonds, significantly improving passivation performance. However, excess hydrogen accumulates at the localized Ag–Si contact interface, deactivating dopants and increasing contact resistivity on both sides after post-annealing of SCs, regardless of whether the TOPCon structure contains the N-dopant or not. A subsequent LECO (laser-enhanced contact optimization) treatment effectively reactivates the dopants and largely restores the electrical properties. These findings provide a foundation for optimizing N-doped TOPCon bottom SCs toward future integration into two-terminal monolithic chalcogenide/silicon tandem devices.

title: Resolving the LiFePO4 Battery State beyond Voltage-Based Diagnostics Using Surface-Scan MRI
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Reliable assessment of state of charge (SoC) and state of health (SoH) in commercial batteries remains a major challenge because their closed architecture obscures the underlying electrochemical, structural, and thermal processes, while existing diagnostic methods often provide only indirect, spatially averaged, voltage-based information about battery operation and degradation. Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) is among the most widely deployed cathode materials due to its low cost, long cycle life, and high thermal stability; however, its characteristically flat voltage profile fundamentally limits the information content of conventional diagnostics. In this work, we exploit the large magnetic-susceptibility contrast between the FP and LFP phases and the lithiation-dependent evolution of their phase fractions for accurate and time-efficient determination of SoC in commercial pouch cells and battery packs. Surface-scan magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides new SoC and SoH metrics through quantitative inside-out measurements of battery-induced magnetic field perturbations. LFP is a cathode material particularly well suited to this approach because its biphasic FP/LFP regime spans a large fraction of the usable SoC window while generating substantial magnetic susceptibility contrast between the FP and LFP phases. Under the biphasic approximation, the average magnetic susceptibility follows the lever rule, predicting a linear relationship between the induced magnetic field offset and SoC. Surface-scan MRI experiments confirm this prediction over a broad SoC range. We further establish a framework for spatial mapping of SoC and SoH heterogeneity in multi-cell architectures representative of practical battery packs. Despite minimal voltage differences between cells, the method enables quantitative visualization of charge imbalance and structural heterogeneity on the timescale of seconds.

title: Trace Bifunctional Diboron Additive Enables Robust CEI/SEI Interphases for Long-Cycling 4.5 V Li||NCM811 Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing efficient, low-cost, multifunctional additives that require small amounts and can simultaneously protect both the cathode and anode remains a major challenge for the practical application of lithium batteries. Herein, bis(2,4-dimethylpentane-2,4-glycolato)diboron (B2hmp2) was introduced to construct a greatly Li+-conductive cathode electrolyte interphases (CEIs) at the LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) surface together with robust solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Using a common electrolyte with 0.2 wt % B2hmp2, the Li||Li cells deliver markedly enhanced long-cycling stability, sustaining stable operation for 500 h at 0.5 mA cm–2. Furthermore, following 350 cycles at 0.5 C, the capacity retention of 4.5 V Li||NCM811 cells was elevated from 57.2 to 83.6%. Experimental results reveal that the thin, uniform, boron-rich CEI generated by B2hmp2 effectively mitigates particle microcracking and restrains the dissolution of transition metal ions. Interface analysis reveals that the modified SEI film enriched with B–O species and LiF facilitates uniform Li plating/stripping without dendrite formation and reduces the continuous parasitic decomposition of electrolyte solvents. This article highlights the value of trace diboron for forming desirable electrolyte interphases to obtain the wonderful long-term cycle performance and rate performance of Li||NCM811 cells.

title: Controlled Presodiation of Sodium‐Ion Cathode via Electron Cloud Engineering
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na 0.44 MnO 2 , where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na 0.44 MnO 2 cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.

title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O 2 ‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO 2+ ) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO 2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O 2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O 2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

title: Bioorthogonal Vitamin C Probes Enable Cellular Profiling and Investigation of Lysine Vitcylation
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Vitamin C is an essential micronutrient, yet its direct chemical engagement with the proteome remains poorly defined. Here, we develop and experimentally benchmark a bioorthogonal probe platform for labeling, profiling, and imaging of lysine vitcylation, a recently identified vitamin C‐derived post‐translational modification, in living cells. Chemoproteomic analysis and fluorescence imaging reveal a candidate vitcylome enriched in nucleolar proteins associated with ribonucleoprotein biogenesis and RNA processing, and reporter‐derived lysine adducts on selected targets were validated by mass spectrometry. Time‐resolved analyses demonstrate that intracellular vitcylation undergoes unexpectedly rapid remodeling, indicating active cellular regulation. Furthermore, a genome‐wide CRISPR‐Cas9 screen identifies glutathione S‐transferase P1 (GSTP1) as an upstream regulator of global vitamin C‐derived protein modification, linking vitcylation remodeling to cellular electrophile handling and redox homeostasis. Collectively, this platform provides a chemical framework for profiling, visualizing, and investigating protein vitcylation in living cells, and reveals vitcylation as a dynamic, spatially organized and regulated metabolic modification.

title: Triaryl Imidazoles as a Hole-Transporting Interfacial Modifying Layer for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The integration of hole-transporting organic interfacial modifying layers (OIMLs) into perovskite solar cells (PSCs) has attracted significant interest due to their ability to improve performance and stability. However, the development of cost-effective and straightforward methods for synthesizing OIMLs remains underexplored. In this work, we present the design and synthesis of two novel bromoaryl-substituted, imidazole-derived OIMLs: 2,4,5-tris(4-bromophenyl)-1H-imidazole (TPIM-Br) and 4,5-bis(4-bromophenyl)–2-(5-bromothiophen-2-yl)-1H-imidazole (DPIM-TBr). We investigated the thermal, optical, and electrochemical properties of the molecules, confirming their potential as OIMLs in PSCs. The computed energy levels and electrostatic surface potentials (ESPs) of these molecules were examined to elucidate the charge distribution and electron density within TPIM-Br and DPIM-TBr. Comprehensive characterization demonstrated that incorporation of the OIMLs enabled more efficient charge extraction and improved perovskite crystallinity. The champion device yielded 25.85% power conversion efficiency for TPIM-Br, compared to the control's 23.32%. This work presents a strategy to enhance the performance of inverted PSCs by incorporating OIMLs, offering a promising pathway for future developments in PSC technology.

title: A Carboxymethyl Cellulose Hydrogel Switch Enabling pH-Responsive Fertilizer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The Green Revolution boosted crop yields with synthetic fertilizers, but their high solubility causes environmental pollution and poor synchronization with crop nutrient demands. To address this problem, we developed green intelligent fertilizers (GIF) using a pH-responsive material to enable root-fertilizer feedback. An ultra-sensitive and biodegradable pH-responsive material (pH-B) was synthesized by coordinating carboxymethyl cellulose with Ca2+ and cross-linking, with H+ sensitivity at 10–4 mol L–1. We then constructed a smart release system by embedding this pH-B switch into a 5% polyurethane coating to encapsulate diammonium phosphate (DAP) granules. In this design, the polyurethane matrix impedes the contact between DAP granules and soil water and thus minimizes phosphorus solubilization, leaching, and fixation, while the pH-B switch acts as an acidity-activated gatekeeper whose shrinking enables water penetration through the coating material. In acidic soil, the shoot P content of faba bean increased significantly (by 37–61%) in the treatment with pH-responsive fertilizer compared with DAP. Consequently, in calcareous soils, these fertilizers release nutrients specifically in response to rhizosphere acidification caused by proton exudation from phosphorus-deficient plant roots. This mechanism precisely synchronizes nutrient supply with crop demand. Our work provides a novel strategy for enhancing nutrient-use efficiency and promoting sustainable agriculture.

title: Confined Liquid Transport Engineering for Compact and High-Performance Microfluidic Transparency-Switching Glass
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Microfluidic transparency-switching glass (MTSG) systems based on liquid-filled cavities offer a promising approach for dynamic control of optical transmission, but their practical implementation is limited by high liquid consumption, slow drainage, and bulky device architectures. Here, we investigate fluid transport in confined microfluidic cavities to establish design principles for efficient transparency switching to a desired level, effectively serving as a built-in curtain. By systematically varying cavity thickness (0–300 µm) and liquid viscosity (1–20 mPa·s), we show that reducing the cavity gap to 100 μm and employing a low-viscosity refractive index matching liquid (RIML), such as methyl benzoate, enables stable liquid curtain formation while reducing liquid consumption. Low-viscosity RIMLs also promote more effective drainage, resulting in enhanced opacity (T = 16.26 ± 0.20%) in the drained state. Dynamic display patterns were achieved, enabling switchable decorative and functional features within the smart-glass assembly. Furthermore, beam-engineering-based theoretical calculations, validated experimentally, were used to determine the maximum viable dimensions of large-area glass panels. These findings provide practical guidelines for the development of compact, energy-efficient, and scalable MTSG systems.

title: Addition and Correction to “Polymer Brush-Assisted Fabrication of Layered Metal Oxide Heterostructures for Future Electronic Device Applications”
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)

title: Sparse Electromagnetic-Compatibility Flexible Electrodes for High-Accuracy, Fast-Recognition Human–Computer Interfaces
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Surface electromyography (sEMG) gesture recognition technology offers significant potential for enhancing human-computer interaction and rehabilitation engineering by providing an intuitive and noninvasive method of engagement. However, challenges such as electromagnetic interference (EMI), signal feature processing, and adaptability to individual variability remain prevalent. To address these issues, this paper presents a comprehensive framework that encompasses material selection, device design, feature selection algorithms, integration strategies, and system layout to create a skin-integrated electronic system functioning as a wireless control interface between humans and machines. This system features a flexible electrode that incorporates fractal design elements, serpentine structures, honeycomb configurations, and multilayer graphene, along with an efficient feature selection algorithm grounded in data dispersion principles. It is characterized by enhanced resistance to EMI, conformal attachment capabilities, rapid motion recognition, and high accuracy. Our work stands out with a dramatically higher shielding efficiency of 99.98% and a classification accuracy rate of 97.8%. This methodology significantly enhances the performance of sEMG-based human-computer interfaces, emphasizing rapid recognition speeds and high accuracy in real-time applications such as remote-control systems and virtual reality environments, thereby broadening its applicability across diverse contexts.

title: A Tumor-Activatable DNA Nanoengager That Orchestrates NK Receptor Clustering and Immune Checkpoint Blockage to Enhance Antitumor Cytotoxicity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Natural killer cell engagers (NKCEs) are promising immunotherapeutic agents for cancer treatment. However, their efficacy against solid tumors is severely limited by immune evasion mechanisms (mediated by the sialic acid–Siglec axis and PD-1/PD-L1 pathway), along with poor pharmacokinetics and off-target effects. Harnessing the precision and addressability of DNA origami, we engineered a tissue-specific, DNA origami-based, dual checkpoint-inhibiting NK synapse engager. This nanoplatform adopts a bilayered barrel architecture: the inner layer is functionalized with aNKp46, aPD-L1, and sialidase, while the outer layer is modified with the serum albumin-binding peptide ABD035 and a pH-sensitive i-motif switch. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the DNA nanoengager undergoes specific dissociation of the outer protective layer, exposing the functional modules. These components concurrently bridge and activate NK cells, block the PD-L1 immune checkpoint, and specifically degrade tumor surface sialic acids, thereby reversing dual immunosuppression. This integrated DNA system enables synergistic integration of targeted activation, dual checkpoint blockade, and tumor microenvironment responsiveness, providing a novel smart nanoscale strategy to overcome multifaceted immune evasion in solid tumors and enhance the safety and efficacy of NK cell-based immunotherapy.

title: Spin Polarization Enhanced Photocatalytic N2 Reduction on Chiral Mesostructured Bi2WO6
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Harnessing the earth-abundant N2 via photocatalysis is a sustainable route to green NH3 synthesis. However, photocatalytic N2 reduction (PNR) remains constrained by the high energy barrier for N2 activation and reduction. In this work, we report that the spin-polarized chiral mesostructured Bi2WO6 (CMB) can facilitate the formation of metastable triplet NOH (3NOH) intermediates, while simultaneously promoting the separation and transport of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby enhancing PNR performance. The CMB was fabricated via a hydrothermal method using tartaric acid as a symmetry-breaking agent. Under sacrificial-agent-free conditions, the NH3 yield of 1325.5 μmol gcat–1 h–1 was achieved, representing a 4.7-fold enhancement over the best values reported for Bi- and W-based catalysts. The pronounced accumulation of the *NOH intermediate, a key precursor to NH3, is speculated to originate from the 3NOH intermediate, driven by the spin polarization of CMB. This work reveals the critical role of spin polarization in regulating triplet reaction intermediates and charge-carrier dynamics during N2 reduction, providing an effective strategy for the design of advanced photocatalysts for sustainable NH3 synthesis.

title: Topological Chemistry of PtPb4 Surfaces under Reconstruction and Hydrogen Adsorption
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Topological materials have recently been proposed as promising catalysts owing to the presence of robust topological surface states (TSSs). However, the microscopic role of TSSs in catalytic processes remains elusive. In particular, it is unclear how TSSs can simultaneously remain robust against chemical perturbations while actively participating in surface reactions. Here, we address this question through a combined study of the bulk topology, surface structure, and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) behavior of PtPb4, a valence analogue of a known topological catalyst PtSn4. We show that PtPb4 is a topological semimetal with non-trivial ℤ2 indices under spin-orbit coupling. This nontrivial band topology originates from a band inversion between two Pb-derived states near the Fermi level. Surface calculations reveal well-defined TSSs on the (100) surface, a surface that also exhibits potential HER properties. Hydrogen binding is primarily achieved by the deep H-1s/Pt-d bonding state located well below the Fermi level, while the TSSs play only a secondary, perturbative role in adsorption. By continuously tracking the evolution of the surface bands during adsorption, we demonstrate that the topological order is preserved despite substantial energy shifts, charge transfer, and hybridization in surface states. Our work provides a qualitative picture of how the TSSs of PtPb4 respond to hydrogen adsorption while the global topology of the surface remains inherently robust.

title: BODIPY-Based Fluorescent Probes for Selected Hazardous Chemicals: Multilevel Regulation of Sensing Performance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rapid and reliable detection of hazardous chemicals in complex environments remains an important challenge in fluorescence sensing. BODIPY dyes and related boron-difluoride fluorophores have attracted considerable attention because of their excellent photophysical properties and highly tunable molecular structures. However, sensing performance depends not only on analyte recognition but also on excited-state processes, intermolecular interactions, aggregation behavior, analyte transport, and practical signal readout. This review examines BODIPY-based fluorescent sensing of selected hazardous chemicals at the molecular level, supramolecular and aggregated-state level, and sensing material and device level, focusing on how regulation at different levels addresses different performance limitations. At the molecular level, recognition unit design, conformational regulation, and boron-center transformation regulate analyte recognition and signal transduction. At the supramolecular and aggregated-state level, noncovalent interactions, aggregation-state regulation, and molecular packing influence emission behavior and signal stability. At the sensing material and device level, interfacial and transport regulation, sensing material construction, and device integration and signal readout improve analyte accessibility and practical detection performance. This review provides a systematic framework for understanding the factors that govern BODIPY-based fluorescence sensing. This multilevel classification facilitates the identification of major factors limiting sensing performance and the corresponding regulation strategies, thereby providing guidance for the rational design and optimization of BODIPY-based fluorescent sensing systems.

title: Flexibility technologies in clean energy systems
source: Nature Reviews Clean Technology
abstract: The transition to clean energy systems is increasing the need to balance variable supply and demand across timescales and sectors. This Review describes different technologies that can enable flexibility in energy systems and assesses trends in their global deployment.

title: High-Fidelity Electrochemistry with Ultraclean Graphene Electrodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electrochemical performance of CVD graphene electrodes has remained inconsistent and often inferior to that of exfoliated graphene, limiting their utility in analytical applications. This variability is widely attributed to structural disorder, but the dominant source remains unclear. Here, we show that amorphous carbon contamination introduced during synthesis is the primary factor governing the electrochemical behavior of CVD graphene. By eliminating this disorder during growth through oxygen-free CVD (OF-CVD), we obtain graphene electrodes that exhibit intrinsic and highly reproducible electrochemical behavior. Compared with conventional and commercial graphene, these electrodes display substantially enhanced heterogeneous electron-transfer kinetics, reduced charge-transfer resistance, and improved detection limits across both outer- and inner-sphere redox systems. Notably, they exhibit consistent anodic peak potentials across wide concentration ranges, nearly eliminating the concentration-dependent potential shifts characteristic of both glassy carbon and commercial/contaminated graphene electrodes. Further, microelectrode array architectures fabricated from this material suppress non-Faradaic background currents and exhibit steady-state diffusion behavior consistent with electrochemical theory, with improved signal-to-noise ratios. Together, these results establish that extrinsic carbon disorder has limited the electrochemical performance of CVD graphene to date. The removal of amorphous carbon reveals defect-free graphene’s intrinsic electrochemical behavior and enables a reproducible, high-performance electrode platform, providing a clear pathway for reliable graphene-based electrochemical systems.

title: A Pathology-Responsive Hydrogel with On-Demand Ion Release for Microenvironment Remodeling and Diabetic Wound Regeneration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The healing of diabetic wounds is often impeded by severe bacterial infections, persistent inflammation, excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and abnormal matrix degradation. Although conventional free silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) possess broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, their inherent tendency to aggregate and inactivate, as well as its high cytotoxicity limits their clinical application. Moreover, a single bactericidal strategy is insufficient to completely reverse the complex pathogenic microenvironment of the wound. To address these challenges, this study developed a dual-polyphenol biomimetic extracellular matrix (ECM) composite hydrogel with matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) and pH-responsive properties, aimed at achieving spatiotemporal precision intervention and active microenvironment remodeling in diabetic wounds. This system employs caffeic acid-modified gelatin and dopamine-modified sodium alginate as a dynamically cross-linked scaffold, incorporated with AgNPs-anchored zinc–aluminum layered double hydroxide (ZnAl-LDH@Ag), that can precisely match the dynamic pathological evolution of the wound. The hydrogel exhibits pathology-adaptive behavior through two complementary mechanisms: gradual MMP-9-mediated remodeling of the gelatin network and infection-associated pH-responsive ion release. MMP-9-mediated degradation enables sustained exposure of ZnAl-LDH@Ag and prolonged matrix remodeling, whereas the acidic microenvironment promotes on-demand release of antibacterial Ag+ and regenerative Zn2+ ions. Additionally, polyphenol moieties provide antioxidant and anti-inflammatory regulation during wound healing. By integrating two-dimensional inorganic layered materials (ZnAl-LDH) with conventional metal nanocrystals (AgNPs), this strategy resolves the clinical paradox in silver-based therapies: the difficulty of balancing high bactericidal activity with low cytotoxicity. In summary, this pathology-driven therapeutic platform enables multimodal synergistic therapy for antioxidant protection, infection control, and tissue regeneration, providing a theoretical foundation and design perspectives for the development of advanced dressings for complex chronic wounds.

title: Rapid Joule-Heating Preparation of GO/GNs Graphene-Based Composite Films for Thermal Management
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Traditional metal heat sinks are limited by moderate thermal conductivity, high density, and poor flexibility, which restrict their use in compact and lightweight electronics. Graphene films offer high in-plane thermal conductivity, but rapid reduction of graphene oxide (GO) releases gases from oxygen-containing groups and can generate pores, interlayer damage, and poor film densification. Here, we report a precursor-design strategy that combines reduced graphene oxide nanosheets (GNs) with carboxylated cellulose nanofibers (CNFs). The composite films (GO/GNs-X) were prepared by blade coating, hot-press carbonization, and secondary Joule-heating graphitization. The combined precursor was designed to mitigate gas-release-induced damage and support carbon-network reconstruction during high-temperature treatment. The optimized GF, with a thickness of approximately 25 μm, reached an in-plane thermal conductivity of 950.5 ± 20 W m–1 K–1 and an electrical conductivity of 2.31 × 105 S m–1. At a comparable thickness, this thermal conductivity was 26.6% higher than that of an additive-free RGO-2600-ref film prepared without GNs/CNF modification. In LED heat-dissipation tests, the surface-centre temperature decreased from 83.7 to 40.4 °C. Because individual-additive controls were not included, the respective contributions of GNs and CNF could not be separated. These results establish combined precursor modification as a route to thin, lightweight graphene heat spreaders. Such films may be useful for thermal management in compact electronics, foldable devices, and aerospace systems.

title: Broadband Electro-Thermal Full-Space Modulation in Freeform VO2 Metagrating in the Telecom Band
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrically tunable metasurfaces for free-space light modulation have been widely studied, with VO2-based phase-change metasurfaces standing out for their large, broadband material tunability and reliable electrical modulation. However, simultaneously modulating both transmitted and reflected beams across a broad bandwidth is a multi-objective problem that is difficult to satisfy with intuitive metasurface designs built on one or a few eigenmodes, calling for complex multimode structures accessible only through inverse design. Here, we demonstrate broadband electro-thermal modulation of both reflected and transmitted beams in an adjoint-optimized freeform Au–VO2 metasurface on sapphire, operating as an amplitude modulator across the telecom bands (1200–1600 nm), with the Au layer serving as both electrode and plasmonic field concentrator. Measurements reproduce the simulated complementary switching of the two channels, yielding band-averaged modulation depths of ∼0.4 (transmittance) and ∼0.7 (reflectance) and optical efficiencies of ∼0.18 (transmittance) and ∼0.15 (reflectance) for y-polarized incidence. A coupled Bloch mode analysis then uncovers how the optimizer meets these competing objectives, the origins of the polarization selectivity, and the broadband nature of the switching. This work establishes adjoint optimization combined with multi-mode analysis as a framework for VO2-based active metasurfaces, opening a route toward compact full-space light modulators for optical communications, interconnects, and free-space optical computing in the telecom bands.

title: Dynamic Diels–Alder-Crosslinked Zwitterionic Polyurethane Coatings with Self-Healing, Antibacterial, and Antifouling Properties
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Coatings used in marine and humid environments are simultaneously exposed to biofouling and mechanical damage, which progressively compromise their interfacial functionality and service stability. In this study, polyurethane resins bearing terminal maleimide groups and sulfobetaine moieties (ZPU-X) were synthesized and subsequently crosslinked with a tetrafunctional furan-terminated compound (TF) through reversible Diels–Alder (DA) reactions to produce dynamically DA-crosslinked zwitterionic polyurethane coatings (SA-X). The sulfobetaine groups promoted the formation of hydrated interfaces that reduced microorganism-coating interactions, achieving maximum antibacterial and antialgal rates of 96.7 and 99.7%, respectively, while effectively suppressing surface colonization by Aspergillus niger (A. niger). The reversible furan-maleimide crosslinks endowed the system with the capacity for segmental rearrangement and network reconstruction. After self-healing, the tensile strength and elongation at break of the coatings reached up to 25.69 ± 0.17 MPa and 1645.13 ± 54.27%, respectively. After 1000 Taber abrasion cycles, the coatings retained liquid-repellent behavior, demonstrating good surface functionality under wear. This work provides an effective strategy for developing functional polyurethane coatings that integrate antibacterial, antifouling, and self-healing properties.

title: Photo-/Electrothermally Gated Slippery-Pore Surface for All-Weather Anti-/De-icing and Meltwater Drainage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Icing threatens the safe operation of aircraft, power facilities, wind turbine blades, and other engineering surfaces. Although existing superhydrophobic, photothermal, electrothermal, and drainage surfaces can individually delay freezing, actively melt ice, or transport liquids, most of them are static designs and therefore cannot simultaneously meet the conflicting requirements of water-repellent anti-icing before freezing and rapid drainage after ice melting. Here, we propose a slippery-pore-based photo–electro dual-mode gated anti-/de-icing surface, termed the porous epoxy actuated electrothermal superhydrophobic (PEAES) surface. In the closed state, the surface maintains superhydrophobic anti-icing properties. Under photothermal or electrothermal stimulation, the PI/graphene scales undergo thermally induced bending and expose the underlying slippery pores, enabling low-residue meltwater drainage. When the pores are blocked by ice, the embedded multiwalled carbon nanotube electrothermal layer can further restore the drainage pathway. The PEAES scales achieved reversible opening within 11 s under 1 sun irradiation and within 8 s under a 5 V electrothermal input. At –10 and –20 °C, PEAES exhibited prolonged freezing delay and a low ice adhesion strength of approximately 6 kPa. Under photothermal, electrothermal, and photo–electro synergistic modes, ice melting was completed within 11, 6, and 3 s, respectively. More importantly, PEAES reduced the residual meltwater after ice melting to nearly zero and decreased the secondary icing area ratio to 0%. This work coordinates anti-icing, de-icing, drainage, and recovery through gated state switching, providing a new structural strategy for adaptive anti-/de-icing and meltwater management across multiple energy-input conditions and successive icing stages.

title: Coupling the Spin State Switching and CO2 Adsorption Operating at Different Temperatures in a Breathing Metal–Organic Framework
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Gas-responsive magnetic response arising from spin-crossover (SCO) phenomena is rare yet highly attractive for molecular sensing and spintronics. However, it remains unclear how gas uptake influences SCO behaviour when the two phenomena occur in separate temperature regimes. Herein, we report a strong influence of CO2 adsorption on the SCO behaviour of a Hofmann clathrate, [FeII(epac)2(PtII(CN)4)]·nEtOH (1·nEtOH, n ≤ 2), despite the two effects occurring at different temperatures. Complex (1·2EtOH) exhibits highly cooperative SCO with a hysteresis width ∼65 K and preserves the framework topology upon desolvation (1). However, hysteresis reduces to 30 K in the guest-free phase (1), underscoring the critical role of lattice solvent in mediating cooperativity. Complex (1) selectively adsorbs CO2 through a gate-opening mechanism at temperatures substantially higher than the SCO region. Despite this mismatch in operating temperatures, increasing CO2 loading progressively stabilizes the low-spin state and shifts the transition temperature (Teq) by ∼20 K. These findings support a delayed guest-mediated coupling mechanism where CO2 first enters the framework at elevated temperatures and subsequently modifies spin-state energetics only after immobilization within the host lattice at lower temperatures. This study establishes that gas adsorption and SCO need not occur within overlapping temperatures to remain strongly coupled.

title: Spray-Freezing-Engineered Cuttlebone Architectures Enable Multiscale Mechanical Reinforcement in Graphene–Cellulose Aerogels
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Graphene–cellulose aerogels offer lightweight and multifunctional platforms, yet their limited mechanical robustness restricts practical deployment. Herein, we report a bioinspired strategy that integrates novel spray-freezing fabrication with a cuttlebone-mimetic wall–septa architecture to achieve multiscale mechanical reinforcement in graphene–cellulose aerogels. The spray-freezing method allows for scalable production, and the resulting aerogels exhibit an ultralow density of 0.077 g/cm3 while achieving a specific strength of 14.80 kN m/kg and specific modulus of 4.51 kN m/kg at 80% compressive strain, corresponding to 4.95 and 4.96 times those of conventional freeze-dried counterparts. Multiscale simulations reveal that the enhancement arises from two primary mechanisms. At the nanoscale, borax-mediated crosslinking enhances cellulose network integrity, while the bending and load redistribution of graphene nanosheets introduce additional energy dissipation pathways within the lamellar framework. At the mesoscale, horizontal septa in the structure effectively relieve stress concentration during high strain compression. The synergistic coupling of molecular reinforcement and architectural stress redistribution establishes a structure-property paradigm for mechanically resilient cellular nanocomposites. This work provides mechanistic insights into bioinspired multiscale reinforcement and offers a scalable platform for engineering high-performance, lightweight graphene-based aerogels, which is expected to be applied in the thermal and fire prevention fields.

title: Gate-Programmable Spectral Plasticity in Nanoporous Vertical Organic Synaptic Transistors for Adaptive Neuromorphic Vision
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Artificial vision systems capable of dynamically adapting to changing spectral environments are essential for next-generation intelligent perception but remain fundamentally constrained by the fixed spectral responsivity of conventional photodetectors. While narrowband photodetectors effectively suppress optical background interference, their spectral selectivity is generally predetermined by material composition or device geometry, preventing adaptive spectral perception within a single hardware platform. Here, we report a nanoporous vertical organic synaptic transistor based on a highly diluted P3HT:PC61BM (100:1) blend that enables gate-programmable spectral plasticity, allowing reversible electrical switching between wavelength-selective narrowband detection and broadband panchromatic perception. Unlike conventional planar phototransistors, the vertically configured transport architecture spatially decouples optical absorption from electrostatic channel modulation, thereby overcoming the long-standing incompatibility between the thick photoactive layers (1.5 μm) required for charge-collection narrowing and the ultrathin semiconductor channels necessary for efficient gate control. By electrically reshaping the interfacial energy landscape and carrier collection length, gate modulation dynamically regulates the extraction of photogenerated carriers across different penetration depths, producing adaptive spectral responses without altering either the material composition or device structure. Quantitatively, the device achieves a competitive R of 41.7 A/W, a shot-noise-limited D* of 2.7 × 1013 Jones, and an EQE of 8.3 × 103%. Beyond spectral reconfigurability, the thick active layer naturally introduces persistent photoconductivity arising from trap-mediated carrier relaxation, enabling biologically analogous excitatory postsynaptic current generation together with paired-pulse facilitation (reaching an index of 290%), spike-number-, spike-duration-, and spike-intensity-dependent plasticity, as well as programmable transitions from short-term to long-term plasticity. These multidimensional synaptic dynamics provide intrinsic temporal information processing directly at the sensor level, eliminating the need for separate sensing and memory units. Furthermore, experimentally acquired synaptic conductance characteristics are integrated into convolutional neural networks through a hardware–algorithm codesign strategy to emulate adaptive retinal signal preprocessing. System-level simulations demonstrate that electrically programmable spectral weighting significantly improves both broadband image recognition and monochromatic color discrimination by dynamically matching spectral perception to different visual tasks. This work establishes a general strategy for integrating adaptive spectral sensing, electrically programmable phototransistors, and neuromorphic information processing within a unified vertical organic transistor architecture, providing a versatile materials platform for intelligent optoelectronic systems.

title: Bioengineered Hybrid Nanovesicles Modulate the Immune Microenvironment with Targeted Drug Delivery for Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Combining chemotherapy and immunotherapy shows great promise for treating esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but its effectiveness is hindered by the immunosuppressive tumor environment and challenges in drug delivery. Recent research has focused on cell membrane-coated nanoparticles for targeted drug delivery, leveraging their ability to evade the immune system while selectively targeting tumor cells. In this study, we developed a biomimetic hybrid nanoplatform based on cell membranes to combine molecular chemotherapy and improve the effectiveness of immunochemotherapy in treating ESCC. The nanoplatform is coated with a membrane fusion of activated neutrophils and ESCC cells and loaded with paclitaxel (PTX) and small interfering RNA targeting EFNA1 (siEFNA1), a molecule linked to ESCC metastasis. By exploiting the homologous targeting properties of ESCC cell membranes and the tumor-homing ability of neutrophil membranes, the platform effectively targets ESCC tissues and delivers siEFNA1 and PTX. This allows for a synergistic treatment approach, combining EFNA1 gene silencing with PTX-induced cytotoxicity to target ESCC more effectively. Crucially, the nanoplatform reprograms tumor-associated macrophages from the pro-tumor M2 phenotype to the anti-tumor M1 phenotype while boosting T cell-mediated cytotoxicity and remodeling the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Overall, this strategy presents a promising approach for the targeted treatment of ESCC.

title: Phenolic Additive-Doped Cathode Interlayer for High-Efficiency Organic Photovoltaics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The cathode interlayer (CIL) is crucial for the development of organic photovoltaics (OPVs). However, the widespread use of CILs based on perylene diimide and naphthalene diimide is constrained by their strong intrinsic aggregation tendency. Herein, benzoic acid (BA) and its derivatives bearing different quantities of hydroxyl groups (BA-OH, BA-2OH, and BA-3OH) are used as additives to modify NDI-Ph, a naphthalene diimide-based cathode interlayer. Systematic studies reveal that the dipole moment of additives rises with the increasing number of hydroxyl groups, which further facilitates intermolecular interactions with interfacial materials. Benefiting from the enhanced electrical conductivity, optimized interfacial contact, and suppressed charge recombination, the NDI-Ph modified by BA-3OH delivers a champion efficiency of 19.20% in D18:L8-BO-based devices, exceeding the 18.25% efficiency of the control device. Furthermore, with 2PACz as the hole transport layer, the device achieves a high PCE of 20.09%. This strategy has also been proven effective for PDINN- and PNDIT-F3N-based CILs. This work verifies that modulating the number of hydroxyl groups in benzoic acid derivatives can rationally regulate the performance of CILs and prescribes a facile and effective strategy to develop high-efficiency OPVs.

title: Multivariate Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework Derived Hollow NiCo2O4 for Selective Alkene Oxidation by Oxygen Vacancy Engineering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective oxidation of alkene to valuable chemical feedstocks is challenging due to the seesaw effect between conversion and selectivity. Here, multivariate zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs) are transformed into bimetallic oxides with varied morphologies via tannic acid (TA) etching and calcination. Impressively, TA etching results in the formation of oxygen vacancies and pore expansion, and the hollow architecture is generated after pyrolysis, favoring the exposure of more active sites and rapid mass diffusion, as well as inducing prominent void-confinement effects. Besides, the incorporation of nickel ions can introduce an additional type of Lewis acid sites into the resulting bimetallic oxides. The obtained Co3Ni1-TA1.4-10-400 exhibits an effective styrene-to-benzaldehyde oxidation with nearly total conversion and a 99% yield (5 h, 90 °C), approximately 1.9 and 8.3 times higher than those of Co3Ni1-TA1.4-10 (51%) and Co3Ni1-O (12%), respectively. Mechanistic investigations for the conversion of styrene to benzaldehyde further indicate that the reaction possibly proceeds via a synergistic mechanism involving both a metal-peroxide pathway and a free-radical pathway. Furthermore, in the presence of sodium bicarbonate, Co3Ni1-TA1.4-10-400 can prove effective in catalytic epoxidation of styrene. This study provides a valid approach for the construction of ZIF derivatives with abundant oxygen vacancies and unsaturated metal sites as promising catalysts for fine and commodity chemical production.

title: Evolution shapes ecosystem resilience through spatial self-organization
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Drylands are globally widespread and ecologically important but vulnerable to climate change. Many exhibit spatially self-organized vegetation patterns that enhance resilience by enabling vegetation to reorganize their patterns under drying, thereby optimizing water use and maintaining productivity. Plants can also undergo evolution in response to environmental change. Although both spatial self-organization and rapid evolution are fundamental mechanisms of resilience, their interaction remains largely unknown. Using a theoretical model, we examine how these mechanisms interact to shape vegetation transitions—abrupt or gradual—and ecosystem resilience under climatic drying. We find that pattern formation can suppress adaptation by maintaining soil moisture beneath vegetation patches despite rainfall decline, thereby limiting selection for increased drought tolerance. However, this suppression is largely alleviated under the variable rainfall typical of drylands. In turn, evolution feeds back on self-organization by increasing the spatial plasticity of vegetation patterns and their ability to reorganize under changing climate, although this positive effect weakens as evolutionary rate increases. Considering direct (adaptation) and indirect (pattern-mediated) effects, evolution enhances resilience, with indirect effects via pattern plasticity dominating. Within model scenarios spanning plausible rainfall variability and relative evolutionary-to-ecological rates, more than half of vegetation transitions are abrupt involving biomass losses exceeding 50%, highlighting a potential mechanism underlying recent global observations of widespread abrupt vegetation losses in drylands. These results demonstrate that evolution and spatial self-organization jointly determine dryland resilience under environmental change and highlight the unexpected role of evolution in patterned landscapes, calling for integrative approaches to predict ecosystem responses in a changing world.

title: Nutrient legacies from elephant megacarcasses create coldspots of biodiversity and hotspots of ecosystem processes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Terrestrial megafauna (animals >1,000 kg) have substantial impacts on ecosystems while alive; yet, we know little about the impacts of these ecosystem engineers after they die. Like whale carcasses in the ocean, terrestrial megacarcasses may leave ecological legacies via the nutrient pulses they create on the landscape. Here, we investigated the impact of elephant megacarcasses on savanna ecosystems in Kruger National Park, South Africa. To determine how elephant carcasses affect below- and aboveground biodiversity and ecosystem processes, we collected soil and plant samples from 40 carcass sites (pairing “on carcass” and “off carcass” samples) ranging from 8 d to 7.7 y postmortem. We found that elephant carcasses released enormous pools of nutrients into savanna soils, increasing ammonium by 31×, nitrate by 7×, and phosphorus by 3× on average. These extreme ammonium concentrations were negatively correlated with the biodiversity of bacteria and plants, which were both suppressed at elephant carcass sites. Despite these decreases in biodiversity, ecosystem processes were strongly elevated at elephant carcass sites, with soil microbial respiration elevated for 1 to 2 y and herbivore grazing >3× higher for 7+ y postmortem. These results demonstrate that elephant megacarcasses generate coldspots of biodiversity but hotspots of ecosystem processes, unveiling a cryptic ecological function of megaherbivores that is extreme in both magnitude and duration relative to carcasses of smaller animals. As humans drive terrestrial megafauna toward extinction, we risk losing not only their ecosystem engineering abilities while they are alive but also the ecological legacies their carcasses create after death.

title: Shedding light on left hippocampal mGlu5 in Alzheimer’s disease
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGlu5) is essential for synaptic plasticity and memory, making it a potential therapeutic target in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). While hemispheric asymmetries in hippocampal function have been observed in AD patients, the lateralized contribution of mGlu5 signaling to cognitive decline remains unclear. Here, we show a physiological left-right asymmetry in hippocampal mGlu5 expression in wild-type mice, with higher levels in the left hemisphere, consistent with previous reports. This physiological asymmetry is lost in two distinct mouse models of AD, the J20 and 5xFAD mice, revealing a hemisphere-specific disruption of hippocampal mGlu5 regulation. Using the light-controllable negative allosteric modulator Alloswitch-1, we show that selective inhibition of left, but not right, hippocampal mGlu5 restores working and short-term memory in AD mice. This finding indicates that altered mGlu5 expression does not simply reflect receptor loss, but rather a dysregulated signaling state that remains functionally relevant and pharmacologically targetable. Left-specific modulation also normalizes pathological downstream signaling, including aberrant Pyk2 and GSK-3β activation and tau hyperphosphorylation, across both hemispheres, indicating a widespread impact of hemisphere-selective intervention. These findings establish a functional lateralization of hippocampal mGlu5 signaling and identify the left hippocampus as a critical site for mGlu5-dependent memory dysfunction in AD. They also highlight the therapeutic potential of region-specific photopharmacology for precise intervention in early AD pathology, providing a strategy for spatially targeted modulation of pathological synaptic signaling in neurodegenerative disease.

title: A water-pinning hot spot drives templated tau aggregation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein, achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured solvation water has been proposed to be a signature of such hot spots at both the tau fibril-end surface and soluble tau monomers. Although jR2R3-P301L tau exhibits a heterogeneous hydration landscape in its intrinsically disordered state, with enhanced water structuring near the P301L mutation site, it is unclear whether a localized hotspot exists at the fibril end surface and surface water facilitates the initial contacts in templated aggregation. Using rapid
                    1
                    H-
                    15
                    N SOFAST-HMQC NMR to track seed-induced aggregation of jR2R3-P301L in real time, complemented by molecular dynamics simulation of fibril surface hydration, we identify a residue-specific pinning hotspot that is prone to dewetting followed by sequential folding and incorporation of the remaining segment in a two-step dock-and-lock process. Site-specific spin labeling further demonstrates that blocking this pinning hotspot disrupts templated aggregation, leading to shorter fibrils. The identification of a dominant pinning site will facilitate the rational design of binders to effectively disrupt fibril extension or serve as diagnostic or therapeutic strategies.

title: Competing presynaptic protein assemblies coordinate basal neurotransmission with homeostatic plasticity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Neural circuits establish a stable basal level of synaptic transmission that is maintained throughout life. When synaptic activity is perturbed, homeostatic mechanisms restore this set point, but how neurons reconcile long-term stability and rapid compensatory plasticity remains unclear. Here, we identify two competing presynaptic multimolecular complexes that control steady-state transmission and homeostatic potentiation and define the molecular switch that enables transitions between these functional states. At
                    Drosophila
                    neuromuscular junction, the transmembrane protein PlexinB (PlexB) and the auxiliary subunit Neto-α regulate both basal synaptic function and homeostatic plasticity. PlexB association with presynaptic KaiR1D/Neto-α receptor complexes modulates channel properties and fine-tunes neurotransmitter release, whereas PlexB signaling with Semaphorin2b (Sema2b) and Neto-α drives homeostatic potentiation. KaiR1D and Sema2b/PlexB compete for a limited pool of presynaptic Neto-α. Motor neurons switch from steady-state transmission to homeostatic potentiation by exchanging KaiR1D/Neto-α/PlexB complexes for Neto-α/PlexB/Sema2b. Critically, Neto-α must dissociate from KaiR1D-containing complexes to initiate the homeostatic response. Variants of Neto-α or KaiR1D that fail to dissociate support normal basal neurotransmission but abolish homeostatic plasticity. These findings demonstrate that dynamic reorganization of competing presynaptic protein assemblies enables neurons to preserve stable baseline transmission while mounting robust compensatory responses to perturbations. Given the widespread roles of presynaptic receptors and Semaphorin/Plexin signaling in synaptic regulation, this mechanism may represent a conserved strategy for balancing stability and plasticity in neural circuits.

title: A Kv4.2-mGluR5 complex drives enhanced depotentiation in a mouse model of improved cognitive flexibility
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Memory updating promotes cognitive flexibility by enabling suppression of outdated information to optimize behavioral strategies in response to a changing environment. While some circuits involved have been identified, the synaptic mechanisms underlying this process remain uncertain. Here, using a recently developed Kv4.2 knock-in mouse model (Kv4.2TA), we identify a metaplasticity in the hippocampus that accompanies an improvement in cognitive flexibility. Mutation of a C-terminal phosphorylation site (T607) in the alpha subunit of the voltage-gated K
                    +
                    channel protein Kv4.2 drives boosted depotentiation of spike timing-dependent long-term synaptic potentiation mediated by mGluR5 receptors, putative constituents of Kv4.2 macromolecular complexes. We found that mGluR5 receptors are required for the improved cognitive flexibility observed in Kv4.2TA mice. These findings reveal a synaptic correlate associated with memory updating in cognitive flexibility and spotlight the Kv4.2-mGluR5 complex as a therapeutic target for disorders characterized by impairments in cognitive flexibility.

title: Phylogenomics confirms Palaeoptera monophyly and illuminates the origin of winged insects
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The origin and early radiation of winged insects (Pterygota) represent one of the most transformative events in terrestrial evolution, yet phylogenetic relationships among their basalmost lineages (Ephemeroptera, Odonata and Neoptera) continue to be a central debate within insect systematics. Here, we present the most taxonomically comprehensive phylogenomic analysis to date, leveraging genomic and transcriptomic data from 101 species, including 16 sequenced ephemeropteran genomes. Employing 1,367 universal single-copy orthologs across two supermatrices, we used concatenation- and coalescent-based frameworks under homogeneous and heterogeneous, and multispecies coalescent models. Our analyses support Palaeoptera monophyly. Although coalescent-based methods initially suggested a Chiastomyaria (Ephemeroptera + Neoptera) topology, subsequent signal dissection and topology tests confirm that the preponderance of genomic signal favors a monophyletic Palaeoptera. Furthermore, we identify incomplete lineage sorting and gene tree estimation error as the primary drivers of previous topological conflicts. Our molecular dating results point to an Early Devonian origin of crown-Pterygota, whereas crown-Palaeoptera first emerged in the Late Devonian. By reconciling molecular evidence with morphological synapomorphies, such as wing-base sclerite homologies, this study provides a coherent framework for the early evolution of winged insects, supports a single origin of wings, and identifies the neopteran wing-folding mechanism as a singular evolutionary innovation.

title: Imaging and recording of synaptic zinc in the brain by covalent chemistry–based semisynthetic biosensors
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Labile zinc ions (Zn
                    2+
                    ) are stored in glutamatergic vesicles at specific excitatory synapses in the central nervous system and released into synaptic clefts in an activity-dependent manner. However, the precise roles of synaptic Zn
                    2+
                    remain unclear due to a lack of tools capable of analyzing Zn
                    2+
                    with synapse-level spatial resolution in vivo. Here, we developed neuroreceptor-based semisynthetic biosensors that function as integrating dosimeters, recording synaptic Zn
                    2+
                    by covalent chemistry in the living mouse brain. Using a chemical knock-in strategy, we introduced activity-based Zn
                    2+
                    probes with distinct affinities into endogenous α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazole-propionic acid or γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptors. These in-brain-constructed Zn
                    2+
                    sensors enabled region-specific mapping of Zn
                    2+
                    in synaptic clefts in the living mouse brain. Imaging-based analyses revealed differences in apparent Zn
                    2+
                    levels at excitatory and inhibitory synapses across hippocampal regions during kainate-induced seizures, providing insights into the physiological and pathological functions of synaptic Zn
                    2+

title: Cell identity competes with surface tension to determine stromal organization in tumor spheroids beyond the CAF shell paradigm
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are often found forming a peripheral stromal barrier around tumors. Here, this paradigm is challenged using microfabricated 3D cancer–CAF spheroid models combined with quantitative magnetic force tensiometry. A surface tension atlas is established for eight cancer cell lines, three CAF populations, and heterotypic tumor–CAF assemblies, spanning nearly two orders of magnitude. Surface tension is first shown to govern spheroid morphology and modulate drug response. Besides, CAFs consistently occupy the highest end of the surface tension hierarchy, predicting core rather than peripheral localization and directly challenging the shell paradigm. Yet confocal imaging reveals not only central accumulation but also complete CAF-tumor mixing, including in spheroids where cancer cells exhibit surface tensions nearly two orders of magnitude lower than CAFs. Surface tension alone therefore fails to predict CAF organization. Instead, the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) state of cancer cells emerges as a major determinant: epithelial-like tumors promote CAF core accumulation, whereas mesenchymal-like states favor persistent mixing. Peripheral CAF localization emerges only under restricted conditions combining high tumor cohesion and sequential stromal recruitment. Together, these results identify surface tension, EMT state, and assembly chronology as joint determinants of tumor–stroma architecture, revealing a context-dependent organization landscape rather than a universal CAF shell.

title: Coordinated transformations of the labyrinth and occiput during the dinosaur–bird transition
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Evolutionary shape changes of the vertebrate semicircular canals (SCCs) are often ascribed to evolutionary transitions in locomotion, including the origin of flight during the dinosaur–bird transition. However, the potential for transformations of braincase architecture to influence SCC shape independent of sensory-functional adaptation has generally been overlooked. We evaluate the influence of both factors using a large dataset of 146 living and recently extinct crown birds, including taxa representing ~24 independent evolutionary losses of flight, together with Mesozoic stem avialans, nonavialan dinosaurs, and pterosaurs. Among crown birds, evolutionary changes in locomotor capabilities, including the total loss of flight, have only weak effects on SCC shape, contrasting with large effects from changes in braincase geometry. Notably, rotation of the occiput toward a ventral orientation is associated with important changes to SCC shape that match those observed during the dinosaur–bird transition. This suggests that evolutionary transformations of SCC shape during the Mesozoic origin of avian flight resulted from evolutionary changes in the orientation of the craniocervical joint, and not from tuning of SCC sensory function. These findings illuminate the importance of integrated morphological changes to the head-neck system during bird origins and challenge the long-standing assumption that SCC morphology enables confident inferences of the locomotor capabilities of extinct vertebrates.

title: Improved assessment of Alaskan Arctic coastal wave exposure accounting for landfast ice
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Simulations of the ocean wave climate are critical for assessment of coastal processes and hazards in observation sparse regions such as the Arctic. While the multidecade wind and ice datasets necessary for driving long-term wave simulations have proven reliable for such efforts, the presence of landfast ice along shorelines at scales not represented by these data has been a persistent uncertainty impeding accurate analysis of impacts to Arctic coasts. Here, we explore this uncertainty by producing a historical high-resolution wave simulation and combining simulation outputs with landfast ice data for the Alaskan Arctic. The resulting dataset yields an improved assessment of coastal waves and identifies stark contrasts in the seasonal wave exposure of the Chukchi and Beaufort regions. Notably, analysis shows that absent supplemented landfast ice, coastal ice cover is broadly underestimated by 10 to 25 d, resulting in wave energy being overestimated by 5 to 10% in shallow depths nearshore. Notably, these figures can reach up to 70 d of underestimation for ice cover and 48% overestimation of wave energy in certain locations. The persistent overestimation and potential for extreme positive biases in coastal wave assessment highlight the need for representation of landfast ice in Arctic coastal analysis efforts and our analysis reveals the spatial and temporal biases for related research.

title: Multidimensional vulnerabilities of informal settlements in the Urban South
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Informal settlements are widespread and rapidly growing, often associated with high vulnerabilities. However, global-scale understanding on their spatial distribution and complexity of vulnerability is limited. Here, we delineate the informal settlements across a sample of 1,914 cities of the Global South by integrating Sentinel-2 imagery with deep learning models, and we explore the heterogeneity of vulnerability using Urban Informal Settlement Vulnerability Index that encompasses living conditions, social infrastructure, and environmental risk. We found that Urban Informal Settlements cover 12.94 ± 2.52% of their total urban areas (approximately 34.04 × 10
                    3
                    km
                    2
                    ), especially in sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Middle Asia. Sub-Saharan African cities have the highest vulnerability of informal settlements, with 31.75 ± 6.20% of total urban areas being occupied by informal settlements, while East Asian cities exhibit relatively low vulnerability across all dimensions. We also find that urban informal settlements with high environmental exposure are widespread in the Global South, and there is a significantly polarized distribution between “low” and “high” vulnerability categories. The findings highlight the disparate distribution of multidimensional vulnerability in informal settlements across the Urban South, providing a comparative evidence base for further local assessment and context-specific policy discussions related to SDG 11.

title: Astrocytic facilitation of somatic NMDARs underpins hippocampal E-S potentiation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: EPSP–spike (E-S) potentiation is a form of plasticity defined by a persistent increase in neuronal spike output for a given synaptic input, reflecting enhanced E-S coupling independent of synaptic strength. However, its cellular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that brief induction of E-S potentiation triggers a sustained calcium activity increase in astrocytes adjacent to the hippocampal CA1 pyramidal layer. Mechanistically, E-S potentiation critically requires GluN2B-containing N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDARs) localized to the neuronal soma. Sustained astrocytic activity promotes E-S potentiation through vesicular release of D-serine, which enhances tonic activation of somatic NMDARs, suppresses A-type potassium currents, and produces a lasting increase in neuronal excitability. Functionally, this astrocyte-dependent E-S potentiation lowers the threshold for subsequent long-term potentiation, conferring a metaplastic influence on hippocampal circuits. These findings identify an astrocyte-neuron signaling mechanism that drives intrinsic plasticity and establish somatic NMDARs as a key site of astrocytic regulation of hippocampal output.
