title: P-body-mediated RNA decay controls neural crest EMT
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Neural crest cells, a multipotent vertebrate stem cell population, undergo a tightly regulated epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) to delaminate from the neural tube and initiate migration. Neural crest EMT is controlled by a transient pulse of
                    Draxin
                    , which acts as a molecular rheostat of canonical Wnt signaling, and is then rapidly downregulated by unknown mechanisms. To address this, here we use in vivo reporter assays and live RNA imaging to show that
                    Draxin
                    mRNA is rapidly degraded posttranscriptionally via its 3′ untranslated region. We found that
                    Draxin
                    transcripts are targeted to cytoplasmic processing bodies (P-bodies), which are membrane-less sites of RNA processing and decay. Disruption of P-bodies by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated depletion of the RNA helicase DDX6 prevented posttranscriptional downregulation of
                    Draxin
                    and impaired neural crest EMT in vivo. These findings parallel observations in human patients carrying
                    DDX6
                    mutations, who exhibit defects in P-body assembly and craniofacial abnormalities associated with neural crest dysfunction. Together, our results identify P-bodies as regulators of
                    Draxin
                    mRNA decay and reveal a spatially organized mechanism of RNA turnover that controls neural crest EMT during vertebrate development.

title: Multiyear dual-isotope fingerprinting at South Asian receptor sites constrains carbon monoxide sources and enhanced oxidation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Carbon monoxide (CO) is an indirect short-lived climate forcer with uncertainties both in sources and its role in atmospheric oxidation. Based on nine winter-long dual-isotope campaigns at two South Asian receptor sites intercepting the continental outflow, we quantified CO source contributions and emission–sink dynamics. Combustion accounts for 68 to 74% of South Asia regional CO (including 34 to 37% from biomass burning) with secondary atmospheric oxidation contributing 26 to 32% (dominated by oxidation of nonmethane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) at 21 to 26%, with methane oxidation contributing 5.5 to 6.4%). These isotope-observational constraints suggest a twice higher role for atmospheric oxidation than in model estimates. Spatially, the absolute contributions of both primary and secondary CO decrease from the Indo-Gangetic Plain to the northern Indian Ocean, while the relative contribution of oxidation-derived CO increases, indicating enhanced secondary CO production near source regions. Observation-model comparison suggests that transport from the continental areas dominates CO over adjacent oceanic regions, with minor local production. During the COVID-19 emission perturbation, combustion-derived CO fell sharply in absolute terms, NMVOC-derived CO rose, and CH
                    4
                    -derived CO remained stable, providing an observational constraint on the sensitivity of atmospheric oxidation to emission changes. Our results reveal a significant contribution of CO from atmospheric oxidation in South Asia, calling for a reassessment of regional emission–oxidation coupling in models and of mitigation strategies.

title: Interfacial microenvironments enable abiotic ribonucleoside formation in micro- and nanoscale compartments
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The abiotic emergence of ribonucleosides remains a central challenge in origin-of-life research because ribonucleosides form inefficiently and are often unstable under prebiotically plausible conditions. Here we show that interfacial microenvironments within aqueous micro- and nanoscale compartments containing D-ribose, phosphoric acid, and nucleobases promote ribonucleoside formation by creating reaction-permissive physicochemical conditions independent of the specific compartment type. Across a diverse range of compartmentalized systems, including gas–oil–water micro/nanobubbles, gas–water micro/nanobubbles, microscale lipid-bilayer vesicles, and oil–water emulsion systems, ribonucleosides form abiotically in the absence of enzymatic catalysis. Under selected interfacial conditions, multiple ribonucleosides, including cytidine, are generated without added catalysts. Comparison among these systems reveals that interfacial architecture and coupled physicochemical properties strongly influence both reaction efficiency and product stability. CO
                    2
                    -based micro/nanobubbles support sustained cytidine accumulation, highlighting the importance of coupled gas–liquid and liquid–liquid interfaces. Ribonucleoside synthesis also depends on compartment size, whereas variations in oil content within micro/nanobubbles selectively modulate inosine formation, underscoring the sensitivity of nucleoside chemistry to interfacial properties. These findings identify interfacial microenvironments within micro- and nanoscale compartments as a general physical framework for ribonucleoside emergence and suggest that ubiquitous compartmentalized interfaces on early Earth could have provided robust settings for prebiotic ribonucleoside chemistry.

title: A multiscale framework for heme crystallization inhibition: From single-molecule step-capping to parasite suppression
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Heme crystallization is central to malaria parasites’ survival during the erythrocytic stage of the disease, yet how clinically relevant antimalarial drugs modulate this process at the molecular level remains unclear. Here we employ stage-resolved parasite assays and multiscale in vitro approaches to explore the interactions between lumefantrine (LF), one of the popular components of current combination therapies, and hematin crystallization. Pulse LF suppresses
                    Plasmodium falciparum
                    during both ring and trophozoite stages. Under biomimetic conditions, LF markedly reduces β-hematin crystal growth rates. High-resolution atomic force microscopy reveals that individual LF molecules bind directly to crystal steps, physically constraining step motion through a previously unreported step-capping mechanism. This localized inhibition propagates to the mesoscale, producing step broadening, reduced interstep spacing, and causing surface kinetic roughening. In contrast to its strong inhibition of crystal growth, LF enhances hematin nucleation by promoting the formation of mesoscopic hematin-rich clusters, as detected by a combination of scattering and microscopy techniques. Attachment of the nucleated crystallites to larger crystal surfaces initiates a nonclassical inhibition sequence by straining the crystal interface, which further impedes step growth.

title: In mice, a population of male germ cells show characteristics of nonapoptotic cell death during G0 arrest
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In mammals, a small population of spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) is established shortly after birth. These cells self-renew and produce sperm for the male’s reproductive lifespan, passing the genome on to the next generation. Establishment of a population of SSCs with high genomic integrity is essential. SSCs are derived from a much larger precursor population of male germ cells (MGCs) that differentiate during fetal life. During the last third of gestation, MGCs undergo a prolonged period of G0 cell cycle arrest during which they sustain high levels of transcription and acquire epigenetic programming for SSC fate. Although these differentiation steps can cause cellular and genomic damage, it has been unclear whether selection for germ cell quality occurs during G0 arrest since no classic markers of cell death have been detected. In this study, we used a mouse model to characterize a population of MGCs that begin to accumulate markers of cell death, such as AnnexinV (AnV) and propidium iodide (PI), at E16.5. The AnV- and PI-positive MGC population is characterized by low expression of the RNA-binding protein, Dead End 1, and exhibits dsDNA breaks and mitochondrial dysfunction. Interestingly, we do not see evidence of an active cell death cascade until the time of birth, when phosphorylation of MLKL, a hallmark of necroptotic cell death, occurs. Based on these findings, we propose that variable cellular health is an important basis for selection of SSC precursors.

title: Heterochronicity shapes brain network formation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Brain network formation unfolds on a nonuniform developmental timetable, with different cortical regions generating connections at different developmental phases. Generative network models (GNMs) aim to uncover the principles underpinning the organization of connectomes by creating synthetic networks according to simple computational rules. These models capture the connectome’s topology, operationalized here as the cumulative distributions of network metrics (e.g., modularity, small-worldness, rich-club structure). However, GNMs typically ignore the differential timing of connectivity formation, and by omitting this temporal programme they often misplace topological features in physical space. Here, we add a heterochronous growth term to GNMs and use a model fitness function that weighs topology and topography equally. Topography refers to the spatial embedding of the network—the actual anatomical positions of the axonal tracts. With these advances, we can generate synthetic networks that more faithfully reproduce the spatial layout of diffusion-MRI connectomes from two independent adult cohorts. Compared with classical, temporally agnostic models, heterochronous simulations improve model fit, accurately locate cortical hubs and modules across individuals, and converge on a single caudal-to-rostral gradient of brain maturation. Overall, integrating heterochronicity makes GNMs more faithful to brain development, and allows for better identification of individual differences in network formation.

title: Antiferromagnetism and tightly bound Cooper pairs induced by kinetic frustration
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Antiferromagnetism and superconductivity are often viewed as competing orders in correlated electron systems. Here, we demonstrate that kinetic frustration in hole motion facilitates their coexistence within the square-lattice repulsive Hubbard model. Combining exact analytical solutions on tailored geometries with large-scale numerical simulations, we reveal a robust pairing mechanism: Holes on opposite sublattices behave as if they carry opposite effective charges due to spin singlet formation from kinetic frustration. This emergent property suppresses phase separation and fosters a coherent
                    
                      
                        d
                      
                    
                    -wave superconducting channel embedded within a long-range antiferromagnetic background. Our findings establish a minimal yet broadly applicable framework for stabilizing strong-coupling superconductivity in doped Mott insulators.

title: Structural insights into the coupling mechanism of vectorial CO2 uptake by DAB1
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:

                    2

                    Thermocrinis albus

Two conformational states define distinct solvent channels for substrate entry and product exit. A suppressor screen identifies mutations that disrupt coupling while retaining CA activity, underlying the importance of conserved residues that link proton translocation to active-site remodeling. These results support a model in which proton-driven conformational changes regulate substrate access to the active site, enabling vectorial CO

title: The honey bee stinger: An unusual pump with collapsible double pistons
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Most stinging animals deliver venom by contracting muscles around a venom reservoir, but honey bees employ a fundamentally different strategy. The stingers of worker bees have the unique ability to autotomize, separating from the body, to continue to sting independently. Despite more than a century of anatomical descriptions, the mechanics of venom pumping have remained unresolved due to the challenges of observing them in action. We recorded high-speed videos of active, autotomized stingers, combined with micro computed tomography-based three-dimensional reconstruction to characterize the biomechanics of stinging in the honey bee
                    Apis mellifera
                    . We reveal that the stinger functions as a unique double-piston micro-pump. Two lancets, each possessing a deformable valve, slide in antiphase within a bulb chamber. These valves dynamically deform to alternately form a seal during the downstroke and collapse during the upstroke, enabling pressure generation for pumping while potentially minimizing backflow during refilling. The inverted tear-drop shape of the bulb facilitates refill even while pumping proceeds. We explored valve deformations and flow behavior by constructing a dynamically scaled physical model of the bulb chamber confirming key features of the pumping cycle and propose mechanisms for valve deformations. The double piston design adds significant design complexity but enables continuous venom delivery in a compact, autonomous unit. These findings provide deeper understanding of venom pumping in honey bees and other Hymenoptera. This study also provides evidence of an axial piston pump within a biological system and offers inspiration for the design of microfluidic pumping devices.

title: Laundering and evasion in response to antislavery policies in Brazil’s cattle sector
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Modern slavery remains pervasive across many economic sectors. Progress toward eradicating it has been partially hindered by a lack of tested, comprehensive policy responses. Using data on millions of cattle transactions in Brazil, we evaluated how ranchers changed their selling behavior after being added to the “Dirty List,” a public registry that names and shames employers found to use modern slavery. Dirty Listed ranchers significantly reduced direct sales to slaughterhouses that signed sustainable supply chain commitments but evaded sanctions by laundering cattle through compliant intermediaries or selling to nonsignatory slaughterhouses. These responses weakened the financial cost of listing to ranchers, and likely allowed beef and leather linked to modern slave labor to enter international supply chains. Our findings highlight the limits of downstream enforcement and underscore the need to monitor upstream suppliers to ensure slavery-free supply chains.

title: Integrating cooperative breeding with reciprocity and culture extends Hamilton’s rule to humans
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: We study how kinship and reciprocity shape giving and child care support in societies with limited access to markets. Extending Hamilton’s rule to incorporate reciprocity, we test it using behavioral data from dictator games and surveys in remote matrilocal and patrilocal villages of northeast India (N = 406 parents of young children). We replicate with data from urban Manila neighborhoods (N = 301) and the Solomon Islands (N = 624). Consistent with predictions, transfers to recipients increase with genetic relatedness to the donor and even more with relatedness to the donor’s child—a hallmark of reciprocity anchored in shared genetic investment. Nonanonymous conditions amplify giving, especially to nonkin. Cultural norms shape cooperation, but do not trump genetic relatedness. These results underscore the role of affinal ties and reciprocal exchange in sustaining cooperation, and suggest a mechanism through which cooperative breeding could contribute to the emergence of generalized reciprocity and human sociality.

title: Nonclassical growth to mesoporous quasi-single crystal CeO2 superstructures with a well-defined surface
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Single-crystal materials are essential for fundamental catalysis studies and advanced technologies; however, synthesizing single crystals that simultaneously integrate mesoporosity, tunable size, and well-defined surfaces remains challenging. Here, we report a wet-chemical, template-free strategy to synthesize mesoporous quasi-single-crystal CeO
                    2

Operando wide- and small-angle X-ray scattering combined with theoretical modeling reveal a nonclassical growth mechanism driven by the oriented attachment of nanocluster building blocks. This process yields high-surface-area quasi-single crystals that preferentially expose energetically favorable (111) facets on both the external surfaces and internal pore walls, thereby enhancing the stabilization of active sites when used as heterogeneous catalyst supports. Using this approach, we demonstrate broad applicability by synthesizing highly dispersed precious metal–loaded CeO
                    2
                    (M/CeO
                    2
                    , M = Pd, Pt, Rh, or Ir) and metal-doped CeO
                    2

                    2

                    2
                    SPs exhibit effective stabilization of Pd clusters in CO
                    2

title: Direct physical contacts with epithelial cells regulate leukocyte actin dynamics to facilitate intraepithelial motility in vivo
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Efficient immune cell migration requires physical interactions with surrounding tissues. While tissue matrix mechanics influence leukocyte motility, it is unknown how leukocytes exert pushing and pulling forces to traverse cell-dense epithelial tissues in vivo. Here, we leverage the optical transparency of larval zebrafish to identify how physical interactions with epithelial cells regulate mechanisms of neutrophil force generation to navigate cell-dense tissues. Confining forces from epithelial cells induce a mechanosensitive central actin network, mediated by Cdc42 and Wiskott–Aldrich Syndrome Protein, which exerts expansile forces on surrounding cells to dilate a path for migration. In concert, direct cell-to-cell (leukocyte–epithelial) contacts mediated by integrin ɑE recognition of epithelial cadherin generate traction forces to enable forward motility. Together, our findings identify how physical interactions with the surrounding cellular environment regulate leukocyte motility through epithelial tissue in vivo.

title: Extensive glacier loss in the coterminous United States
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Glaciers populate the mountain ranges of the western conterminous United States and despite their importance to alpine hydrology, their area and volume change have never been comprehensively evaluated. Our study shows that since the mid-twentieth century about one-quarter of the glaciers have disappeared and the overall area and volume are reduced by one-third. The pattern of glacier shrinkage suggests most glaciers in the conterminous United States are largely maintained by local topographic influences due to their small size. These results improve our understanding of evolving high alpine hydrology and importance to ecosystem processes.

title: Field experiments predict ecological response to a large-scale epidemic of an anti-keystone pathogen
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Knowledge of how pathogens, in the context of a changing environment, shape the structure of ecological communities remains limited, and little information exists on the ability of small-scale field experiments to predict the consequences of large-scale environmental impacts. We addressed these issues using the emergence of a widespread epidemic (sea star wasting disease, SSWD) on rocky intertidal shorelines. Prior experiments demonstrated strong reductions in sessile species diversity in response to the local experimental removal of the sea star
                    Pisaster ochraceus
                    [R. T. Paine,
                    Am. Nat.
                    100
                    , 65–75 (1966); R. T. Paine,
                    Oceologia
                    15
                    , 93–120 (1974)] at our site. In surveys of sea star populations over 8 y spanning the onset of the SSWD epidemic,
                    P. ochraceus
                    populations declined by 90%, then subsequently recovered to about one third of pre-epidemic size under an endemic disease phase. Using four different types of temporal data, we documented large increases in populations of the competitively dominant mussel
                    Mytilus californianus
                    following
                    P. ochraceus
                    decline, which were of similar magnitude to those observed in prior field experiments. As in the field experiments, sessile species richness and diversity declined strongly following the onset of the SSWD epidemic as mussels were released from predator control. Our results reveal a strong effect of a pathogen in regulating ecological community structure by disrupting the role of a keystone species, a result anticipated by prior small-scale field experiments.

title: Double periodicity of the AnkyrinG-associated complex in the axon initial segment
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The axon initial segment (AIS), situated within the first 20 to 60 µm of the axon, is essential for action potential generation and maintenance of axonal identity [M. N. Rasband,
                    Nat. Rev. Neurosci.
                    11
                    , 552–562 (2010)]. Its structure relies on the beta (β)-IV-spectrin/AnkyrinG (AnkG) scaffold arranged periodically underneath the plasma membrane, harboring diverse membrane proteins [K. Xu, G. Zhong, X. Zhuang,
                    Science
                    339
                    , 452–456 (2013); K. L. Hedstrom, Y. Ogawa, M. N. Rasband,
                    J. Cell Biol.
                    183
                    , 635–640 (2008)]. Although a ~190-nm cytoskeletal periodic organization is well established, the precise stoichiometry and spatial arrangement of AIS proteins within the ~190-nm spatial period remain rudimentary, mostly for lack of sufficient spatial resolution and labeling efficiency. Here, using expansion microscopy and cryoelectron tomography, which overcome these technical limitations, we present data on the organization of the AnkG-associated complex within the ~190-nm spatial period. We demonstrate that exactly two AnkG molecules are situated within each period and with their C termini separated by ~80 nm. By contrast, the AnkG-associated cell-adhesion protein neurofascin-186 appears in clusters of varying sizes that are consistent with the periodic organization of AnkG pairs, yet suggesting a more complex molecular arrangement between the two molecules. Altogether, our approach provides insights into AIS molecular organization and protein stoichiometry.

title: Learning dissipative chaotic dynamics with boundedness guarantees
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Chaotic dynamics, commonly seen in weather systems and fluid turbulence, are characterized by their sensitivity to initial conditions, which makes accurate prediction challenging. Recent approaches have focused on developing data-driven models that attempt to preserve invariant statistics over long horizons since many chaotic systems exhibit dissipative behaviors and ergodicity. Despite the recent progress in such models, they are still often prone to generating unbounded trajectories, leading to invalid statistics evaluation. To address this fundamental challenge, we introduce a modular framework that provides formal guarantees of trajectory boundedness for neural network chaotic dynamics models. Our core contribution is a dissipative projection layer that leverages control-theoretic principles to ensure the learned system is dissipative. Specifically, our framework simultaneously learns a dynamics emulator and an energy-like function, where the latter is used to construct an algebraic dissipative constraint within the projection layer. Furthermore, the learned invariant level set provides an outer estimate for the system’s strange attractor, which is known to be difficult to characterize due to its complex geometry. We demonstrate our model’s ability to produce bounded long-horizon forecasts that preserve invariant statistics for chaotic dynamical systems, including Lorenz 96 and a reduced-order model of the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation.

title: AI-generated language remains systematically distinguishable from human communication
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in the social sciences to simulate human behavior and communication, yet validation methods for these applications remain limited. Existing evaluations often rely on human judgments of plausibility, a coarse, difficult-to-scale, and often unreliable benchmark for distinguishing AI-generated from human text. As a result, researchers lack robust tools for assessing the realism of LLM-generated language and for calibrating models to real-world data. We address this gap in two ways. First, we introduce the Conversational Human Authenticity Test (CHAT), a validation framework that combines aggregate metrics of detectability and semantic similarity with interpretable linguistic features, including stylistic markers and topical patterns, to assess how closely LLMs approximate human language in a given dataset. Second, we benchmark nine open-weight LLMs across five calibration strategies, including fine-tuning, stylistic prompting, and context retrieval, on user interactions from X, Bluesky, and Reddit. We find that even after calibration, LLM outputs remain clearly distinguishable from human text, especially in affective tone and emotional expression. Instruction-tuned models generally underperform base models, and larger models do not obviously improve human-likeness. We also identify a trade-off between realism and semantic fidelity: methods that make outputs seem more human often move them further from the content of human responses. Together, these results provide a scalable framework for validation and calibration in LLM-based social simulation while underscoring current limits in reproducing human communication.

title: Disruption halo currents and voltages measured on the HBT-EP tokamak
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: This paper presents measurements of disruption halo currents on the High Beta Tokamak—Extended Pulse (HBT-EP) experiment using 4 high-field side (HFS) tile arrays spaced at equal intervals of toroidal angle. Current flow through the tiles is measured using Rogowski coils external to the tokamak vessel. Tiles can also be operated as floating probes measuring their voltage with respect to the local chamber. Poloidal and toroidal distributions of halo currents are presented, along with a description and explanation of voltage measurements for both axisymmetric and rotating halo currents. Arcing on tiles generates current to components that greatly exceeds ion saturation current limits in the presence of an intact sheath. Furthermore, arcing is observed to occur more frequently as halo current magnitude increases. Measurements of voltages by operating tiles in floating configuration are found to be consistent with the halo voltage generation model presented in Boozer (2013 Phys. Plasmas20 082510). The dependence of tile polarity on poloidal position as well as halo current peak shape are explained using tile voltage measurements.

title: Electronic effects on sputtering of fusion materials under light ion impact
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Understanding material behavior under ion bombardment is a crucial aspect in predicting material surface modification and the lifetime of plasma-facing materials in fusion devices. Atomistic simulations are commonly employed to calculate key ion irradiation outcomes such as sputtering and reflection yields. However, within this simulation framework, the energy dissipation of ions in the electronic system is often neglected or treated using a simple velocity-dependent friction force. Although this approximation can be adequate for slow heavy ions, light ions in the sub-keV range lose a substantial fraction of their energy to electronic excitations, requiring a more realistic energy transfer description. Here, we incorporate trajectory-resolved electronic stopping obtained from ab initio calculations into molecular dynamics simulations of hydrogen and helium irradiation of tungsten and iron. We show that density-dependent electronic stopping leads to systematic variations in sputtering yields, especially for tungsten and lower impact energies, whereas reflection yields are found to be largely insensitive to the model choice. Material-dependent features are identified and mainly attributed to different relative contributions of projectile and recoil electronic energy loss. This work provides a physically motivated approach to improve the accuracy of the sputtering data used in plasma-surface interaction modeling.

title: Calculation of the electromagnetic radiation emitted from the D–T fusion process in tokamak reactors
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: In the deuterium tritium (D–T) fusion reaction an alpha particle is released with the kinetic energy . Since the fusion reaction is governed by the strong interaction, the alpha particle is almost instantaneously accelerated to the final state with its kinetic energy . According to the classical electrodynamics, electromagnetic radiation should be emitted in such an acceleration process. In this work, we calculate the electromagnetic radiation in the D–T fusion process using both the classical electrodynamics and the quantum mechanical models. The radiation is compared with the radiation from the core plasma bremsstrahlung for pure D–T plasmas in large tokamaks. The ratio between the radiation from the D–T fusion reaction and bremsstrahlung depends only on the plasma temperature. The radiation from the D–T fusion reaction is stronger than that from bremsstrahlung if the frequency is higher than a critical value. Although the predicted radiation is much weaker than its high frequency counterpart, it is still possible to be detected in the high fusion gain reactors under some circumstances. Its effect should also be taken into account if one uses the gamma-ray emission spectrum to diagnostic for plasma profiles in tokamaks.

title: A novel high-performance confinement regime in a tokamak driven by tearing mode locking and rotation shear
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: In magnetically confined fusion plasmas, tearing mode (TM) locking is conventionally regarded as detrimental, often halting rotation and triggering disruptions. Contrary to this expectation, we demonstrate that locked TMs can enhance confinement by inducing an internal transport barrier (ITB). Specifically, the interaction between a locked outer plasma region and neutral beam injection (NBI)-driven core rotation generates a broad and intense toroidal velocity shear layer, which suppresses turbulence and improves core confinement. Beam emission spectroscopy and charge exchange recombination spectroscopy confirm a substantial reduction in turbulent transport and a rise in core ion temperature exceeding . This phenomenon—termed the Locking-Induced Flow and Transport (LIFT) mode—transforms a traditionally disruptive mechanism into a confinement enhancement strategy.
