title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

title: An inspiration-off attractor supports the robust and flexible control of breathing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Breathing is a fundamental motor rhythm necessary to sustain life. The rhythm and pattern of breathing arises from the coordination of a rostrocaudally extended ventral respiratory column (VRC) in the medulla. Although recurrent excitation is sufficient for rhythmic bursting in reduced in vitro preparations, comparatively less is understood about how inhibition and excitation interact with feedback circuits to generate the breathing rhythm in vivo. Here, we expand on the classical “inspiratory-off switch” model that inhibitory signaling from lung stretch afferent pathways plays a critical role in generating the breathing rhythm in vivo. We perform high-density extracellular recordings along the length of the VRC during optogenetic and physiological manipulations and apply computational analyses to characterize how these perturbations govern low-dimensional neural dynamics. We show that stimulation of GABAergic afferents of the nucleus of the solitary tract advance or delay breathing in a manner similar to, but quantitatively distinct from, inhibition local to the VRC. We use generative dynamical models to show that inhibitory activity controls respiratory activity through transient stabilization of an attractive region of the low-dimensional manifold corresponding to expiration. Together, these results propose an “inspiratory-off attractor” model that underlies network level control of breathing in vivo.

title: Bioinspired supramolecular thermistor for resolving subtle temperature variations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Precise detection of subtle temperature variations under cryogenic conditions is critical for environmental monitoring but remains challenging because conventional thermistors suffer from limited sensitivity and mechanical interference. Here, we report a bioinspired supramolecular thermistor that achieves thermal transduction through molecularly gated charge transport. The hybrid polyurethane/carboxymethyl cellulose (PU/CMC)/MXene/NiO composite integrates dynamic hydrogen-bond reconfiguration, hydrated ionic conduction, and temperature-dependent electronic transport. Upon cooling, cooperative supramolecular evolution continuously modulates coupled ionic and electronic pathways, producing an ultrahigh negative temperature coefficient of −22,280% °C
                    −1
                    between −80° and −75°C. The thermistor resolves detectable temperature changes below 0.01°C while maintaining negligible hysteresis, excellent reproducibility, and effective thermal-mechanical decoupling. Combined with a dedicated low-noise readout circuit, it enables reliable monitoring of subtle temperature evolution during simulated atmospheric cooling. Integrated into a multichannel sensor array, it further provides force-independent thermal mapping for robotic manipulation. This work establishes molecularly gated supramolecular thermal transduction as a strategy for ultrahigh-resolution cryogenic temperature sensing.

title: Vitamin D binding protein in ventral CA3 of the hippocampus drives stress-induced depression
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The ventral hippocampus plays a crucial role in regulating emotional and motivated behaviors. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its dysfunction in major depressive disorder (MDD) remain poorly understood. Here, we identified elevated expression of vitamin D binding protein (VDBP) in the hippocampi of chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)–susceptible mice, which correlated with the severity of depression-like behaviors. Notably, VDBP up-regulation was specifically in ventral CA3 excitatory (vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    ) neurons. CA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    VDBP overexpression led to inhibited neuronal activity, synaptic and dendritic impairments, and, ultimately, depression-like behaviors. Conversely, vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    -specific VDBP knockdown enhanced resilience to chronic stress. Mechanistically, VDBP directly interacted with PIK3R3 to inhibit the PI3K-Akt-mTOR pathway in a cell-autonomous manner, leading to excessive autophagy and subsequent neuronal dysfunction. Chemogenetic activation, intervention using the Akt-specific activator SC79, and site-specific mutation disrupting the VDBP-PIK3R3 interaction ameliorated vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    VDBP-induced depression-like phenotypes. Collectively, these findings underscore the critical involvement of vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    neuron–derived VDBP in stress-induced depressive pathology and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for MDD.

title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
In most cells,
                    Malat1
                    long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons,
                    Malat1
                    is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

title: Bedrock erodibility governs transient erosion and CO2 release in alpine landscapes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. However, the difficulty of measuring denudation rates in fine-grained rocks has limited our ability to quantify the magnitude of erodibility differences between weak sedimentary and strong igneous rocks. Here, we combine newly developed cosmogenic beryllium-10 measurements in shale with conventional beryllium-10 measurements in intrusive rocks, topographic analysis, solute data, and landscape evolution modeling in the East River watershed, Colorado. Shale-dominated catchments denude three times faster than adjacent intrusive catchments despite having gentler topography. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering–driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain.

title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone. Consistently,
                    tic
                    mutants were hypersensitive to salt stress yet displayed enhanced salt tolerance under 21-hour light-dark cycles matching their shortened circadian period, highlighting the importance of circadian clock in salt tolerance. Salt stress increases H3K9ac levels at the salt stress–responsive genes and induces their expression in a time-of-day–dependent manner in wild-type plants, whereas both H3K9ac level and transcriptional activation are attenuated in
                    tic
                    mutants. TIC physically associates with HD2-type histone deacetylases, and a subset of HD2 partially colocalizes with TIC condensates in the nucleolus under salt stress. Genetic and biochemical analyses showed that salt stress promotes TIC condensate formation, accompanied by reduced HD2 occupancy at salt stress–responsive loci, thereby elevating H3K9ac levels and promoting gene expression. Together, these findings uncover a mechanism by which salt-induced TIC condensate formation links chromatin regulation with circadian timing, thereby promoting plant adaptation to salt stress.

title: Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine Klebsiella pneumoniae neonatal sepsis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Klebsiella pneumoniae
                    is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children.
                    K. pneumoniae
                    isolates are becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, creating a great need for additional therapies or preventative strategies. Maternal vaccination serves as an attractive approach to protect from
                    K. pneumoniae
                    neonatal sepsis. Herein, we report a murine model of maternal immunization followed by pup challenge to evaluate putative
                    K. pneumoniae
                    vaccines. Dams were immunized with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugate vaccines at mating and boosted with two different immunization schedules throughout the gestational period. After parturition, offspring were tested for antigen-specific antibody levels and later challenged with a lethal dose of
                    K. pneumoniae.
                    Pups born to dams immunized with K1- and K2-conjugate vaccines demonstrated significant protection from sepsis relative to control pups. Antibodies transferred from vaccinated dams persisted and remained protective in pups for at least six weeks after birth. Collectively these results demonstrate a feasible and reproducible murine model of maternal immunization verifying the efficacy of bioconjugate vaccines in protecting against lethal neonatal
                    K. pneumoniae
                    infection.

title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

title: Comprehensive characterization of transposable element expression reveals regulatory circuitry and clinical implications in cancers
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute nearly half of the human genome and have crucial roles in regulatory networks and clinical utility in cancers. However, the expression profiles at a single-element resolution remain unexplored. By integrating multiomics data from ∼10,000 samples and 1000 cancer cell lines, we established an expression atlas of 95,512 individual TEs across 980 subfamilies. Transcription factors and RNA binding proteins that are broadly associated with expressed TEs were involved in cancer-related signaling pathways (e.g., MYC activity). We identified 264,252 TEs as putative cis-regulatory elements associated with oncogenic pathways such as inflammatory response. We analyzed alterations in TE expression in tumors and their associations with clinical relevance and responses to more than 1000 anticancer drugs. Last, we developed the Atlas of Transposon Expression in Cancer (ATEC), a TE data portal enabling users to explore TE expression patterns, putative regulatory networks, and clinical significance. Overall, this study established a comprehensive resource for TEs across cancer types.

title: Deep hydrous melting of the mantle wedge recorded by Mg isotopes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. Here, we challenge this view using Mg isotopic data from Nicaragua, the South Sandwich Islands, and the central-eastern Aleutian arc, integrated with a global arc magma compilation. We show that heavy Mg isotopic signatures in mafic arc magmas vary with indicators of volatile enrichment, pointing to a volatile-rich source, most likely the heavily metasomatized base of the mantle wedge. The heaviest Mg isotopic compositions occur in arcs underlain by the most steeply dipping subducting slab, suggesting a focusing effect by the geometry of the downgoing slab. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle.

title: Seabirds and native vegetation drive ecosystem processes that support atoll island resilience
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Ecosystem restoration is expected to enhance ecosystem resilience to climate change, but few empirical and mechanistic demonstrations of such assertions exist. Here, we explore this topic for tropical atoll systems, combining science on nutrient subsidies and geo-ecological functions through a unifying ecological energetics lens. We show that native forest cover and seabird nutrient inputs increase primary productivity and secondary metabolism on islands and adjacent coral reefs, scaling with key ecosystem processes. We then demonstrate that seabird and native forest restoration could contribute to reducing island climate change vulnerability by (i) increasing reef accretion rates such that they keep pace with sea-level rise under a 2.0°C warming scenario, (ii) enhancing the production rate of sediment, which could contribute to island maintenance, and (iii) increasing vegetation fine root length, aiding island sediment stabilization. Collectively, our findings provide an integrated energetics and geo-ecological perspective that suggests rewilding of atolls can contribute to climate resilience.

title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene’s largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. We address this gap in knowledge by using statistical models to infer the demographic and environmental impacts of the Kikai-Akahoya (K-Ah) eruption on Jomon foraging communities occupying the Japanese archipelago. Traditionally framed as an apocalyptic “forcing” mechanism that changed the direction of Japanese prehistory, our results identify a more complex and contingent suite of demographic outcomes. Although we do find evidence of major population collapse in immediately adjacent regions to the volcano, some proximal populations actually increased after the catastrophe, whereas some distal communities were affected by environmental consequences that have hitherto been overlooked. Demographic perspectives on ancient disasters are useful in generating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes.

title: A transcriptional cofactor GRIP1 drives PPARγ DNA binding and p300-dependent enhancer activity during homeostatic macrophage polarization
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Homeostatic macrophages maintain tissue health and resolve inflammation. Upon sustained exposure to type II cytokine IL4, transcription factors STAT6, KLF4, EGR2 and a ligand-regulated nuclear receptor PPARγ orchestrate the M2
                    IL4
                    ‘polarization’, marked by enhancer RNA (eRNA) production near multiple M2 genes. The mechanisms of enhancer activation by unliganded PPARγ are poorly understood. We interrogated cofactor requirements for PPARγ-driven gene expression in M2
                    IL4
                    , including those lacking PPARγ or a ligand-dependent nuclear receptor coregulator NCoA2/GRIP1 vs. macrophages treated with the PPARγ agonist rosiglitazone. As expected, rosiglitazone activated conventional PPARγ targets; GRIP1 deletion blunted their induction and depleted GRIP1-interacting histone acetyltransferase p300 from PPARγ-bound sites. Surprisingly, GRIP1 colocalized with unliganded PPARγ in M0 and M2
                    IL4
                    , and GRIP1 ablation dramatically reduced genome-wide DNA binding of PPARγ itself while promoting broad deposition of CTCF insulator. Functionally, GRIP1 deletion mirrored PPARγ deficiency, establishing GRIP1 as a central regulator of unliganded PPARγ DNA binding, required for both eRNA and mRNA transcription of PPARγ targets in homeostatic macrophages.

title: Reversible Atlantic overturning despite continued Greenland ice sheet melt
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is considered vulnerable to irreversible weakening or collapse under global warming and related Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) melt, yet its resilience to either forcing remains poorly constrained. Here, we use a carbon dioxide emission–driven Earth system model with an interactive GrIS to assess AMOC reversibility under a range of idealized carbon dioxide emission pathways that produce near-linear global warming up to 10 kelvins (K), stabilization across 1.5 to 9 K, and subsequent cooling. We find that although the AMOC reaches threshold-defined collapsed states, these do not represent dynamical tipping in this model: The overturning weakens quasi-linearly with global mean temperature increase yet consistently and promptly recovers under cooling. In contrast, GrIS mass loss accelerates with warming, continues through stabilizations, and is only slowed by cooling, committing the planet to long-term sea level rise. These results reveal contrasting resilience across climate system components: Under transient carbon dioxide forcing, AMOC strength remains dynamically reversible despite continued Greenland meltwater input, whereas the GrIS is locked into persistent decline. Our findings underscore the urgency of rapid emission cuts to limit climate overshoot, AMOC weakening, and irreversible ice sheet loss.

title: Learning to infer transitively on a mental line in premotor cortex
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Transitive inference (TI) is a form of deductive reasoning that enables the derivation of unknown relationships among premises. It is hypothesized that this cognitive process relies on mapping stimuli onto a “mental line,” a linear workspace organized by arbitrarily assigned ranks. However, its neural basis remains unclear: Does this mental line have a neural correlate and how is it learned? This study investigates the role of dorsal premotor cortex (PMd) in encoding the hypothesized mental line as monkeys acquire item relationships for motor decisions. Findings reveal that PMd multiunit activity organizes along a theoretically predicted direction, supporting a geometrical model that explains behavior. Moreover, a learning process is observed, where the mental line rotates to align with motor planning.

title: A fast and frugal Gaussian boson sampling emulator
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Classical algorithms have successfully reproduced expectation values of observables for certain quantum circuits using off-the-shelf computing resources; however, matching the performance of the most advanced quantum devices on sampling problems typically incurs extreme memory and computational costs, restricting such simulations to only a handful of supercomputers worldwide. In this work, we demonstrate a classical simulation outperforming Gaussian boson sampling experiments of 100 modes on established benchmark tests using a single central processing unit (CPU) or graphics processing unit (GPU). Being embarrassingly parallelizable, a small number of CPUs or GPUs allows us to match previous sampling rates that required more than 100 GPUs. We believe that algorithmic and implementation improvements have the potential to generalize our tools to photocounting and pseudo–photon number–resolving scenarios and larger system sizes. Last, most of the innovations in our tools remain valid for generic probability distributions over binary variables, rendering them potentially applicable to the simulation of qubit-based sampling problems and creating classical surrogates for classical-quantum algorithms.

title: A “Progenitor Cell Ark” hydrogel system for intervertebral disc regeneration via mitochondrial targeting and mitophagy enhancement
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), driven by progenitor cell loss and oxidative stress, remains a major clinical challenge with limited effective regenerative therapies. Here, we present a “Progenitor Cell Ark,” a triple-layered hydrogel microsphere system designed for synergistic cell delivery and microenvironment remediation. The Ark comprises an outer nucleus pulposus progenitor cell (NPPC) layer for cell replenishment, a middle GelMA/HAMA scaffold for support, and an inner SS31-modified ultrasmall Prussian blue nanozyme (SS31-UPN) layer that specifically targets mitochondria to scavenge ROS and promote mitophagy. In vitro, SS31-UPN effectively protected NPPCs from oxidative damage, restored mitochondrial function, and enhanced mitophagy. Critically, in severe IVDD rat models, the Progenitor Cell Ark significantly improved intervertebral disc structure, promoted neo-tissue formation, and restored biomechanical function, outperforming cell or bioscaffold therapy alone. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that SS31-UPN’s mitochondrial targeting enhances mitophagy, drives ECM and energy metabolic remodeling, and preserves NPPC stemness, thereby creating a proregenerative milieu. This integrated “cell-in-a-box” strategy offers a robust platform for reversing IVDD and holds notable translational potential for regenerative medicine.

title: Remote allosteric control of single-atom Cu sites in Zr-MOFs enables selective CH4 hydroxylation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Highly selective oxidation of methane to liquid oxygenates under mild conditions remains challenging because of the difficulty in controlling overoxidation at highly reactive sites. Here, we demonstrate remote control of single-atom Cu reactivity through outer-shell coordination engineering in Zr-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). By anchoring Cu
                    1
                    to Zr-oxo nodes in UiO-66-X (X = -NO
                    2
                    , -H, and -CH
                    3
                    ), remote X-BDC ligands systematically modulate the electronic properties of Cu
                    1
                    sites and the catalytic microenvironment. In situ characterization combined with ab initio molecular dynamics in an explicitly solvated aqueous environment reveals a dynamic outer-shell-to-inner-shell regulation that reshapes the active structure and reactive oxygen species around Cu
                    1
                    sites, thereby facilitating CH
                    4
                    activation. In particular, the electron-withdrawing NO
                    2
                    -BDC ligand creates electron-deficient Cu
                    1
                    -
                    •
                    OH* sites, while adsorbed water further regulates active-site conformation. Consequently, Cu
                    1
                    /U6-NO
                    2
                    achieves a turnover frequency of 322.4 h
                    −1
                    with nearly 100% oxygenate selectivity under mild conditions, establishing a general strategy for overcoming activity-selectivity trade-offs in methane conversion.

title: Plasmonic metasurface microfluidic accelerates redox reactions for rapid phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Electron-accepting chain reactions play crucial roles in diagnostics for bacterial infections, from nucleic acid amplification for bacterial identification to metabolic assays for phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing. When coupled with redox mediators, these reactions can be interrogated using an electroanalytical method. We demonstrate kinetic acceleration of loop-mediated isothermal amplification–based identification and resazurin-based phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility profiling through enhanced electromagnetic fields and modulated hot electron injection at the multilayered plasmonic metasurface-fluidic interface. We systematically investigate rounded versus sharp-apex plasmonic architectures, quantifying near-field magnitude and decay to identify geometries that maximize kinetic amplification under electrochemical readout. This approach is further combined with machine learning–assisted Gaussian fitting to improve data quantification and interpretation. Across diverse bacterial species, we achieved rapid identification with no cross-reactivity and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing without overnight culture. In a prospective pilot clinical study of urine specimens directly from patients with suspected urinary tract infections, we observe high accuracy and strong essential and categorical agreement with standard clinical microbiology assays for bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe the underlying mechanisms of spectral tuning. Two mid-wavelength rhodopsins preferentially absorb blue light and a majority of long-wavelength opsins absorb in the green range, but three absorb light beyond 600 nanometers, representing exquisite far red–sensitive animal rhodopsins. Several blue and red rhodopsins exhibit photoreversibility with opposite spectral shifts explained by retinal binding interactions, revealing unrecognized photochemical flexibility in stomatopod photoreception. Row-specific spectral sensitivity results from combining carotenoid filters with multiple individually tuned rhodopsins, altogether extending broad vision to the far-red spectrum.

title: Rewilding the atoll engine
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Seabirds and native forests reconnect ocean, reef, and island processes, strengthening the physical foundations of atoll resilience.

title: Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods. We introduce HAIKA (Hierarchical Attention-based Interpretable K-dimensional Autoencoder), a self-supervised residual channel-attention autoencoder that extracts continuous morphological representations from unlabeled standardized images and highlights the image regions that contribute to those representations. Applied to insect forewings across broad pterygote lineages, HAIKA outperformed most baseline deep learning models and conventional descriptors in clustering, dimensionality reduction, and morphological embedding. When applied to Hymenoptera (i.e., ants, bees, and wasps), the HAIKA-derived continuous characters improved morphology-based phylogenetic reconstruction and illuminated the evolutionary dynamics of wing shape and venation. Our results reveal that wing morphological evolution in Hymenoptera proceeds at decoupled rates across shape and venation modules and is not consistently aligned with key ecological transitions such as parasitoidism or eusociality. HAIKA provides a scalable, image-based route for phenotypic analyses, broadly applicable across diverse taxa and to both 2D and 3D datasets.

title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. Laboratory experiments with ozone alone drove first-order SQ loss and humidity-dependent emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). In contrast, exposure to both ozone and
                    •
                    OH produced nonexponential SQ decays, higher ROS yields, a much stronger in-film
                    •
                    OH source, and condensed-phase products enriched in highly oxidized organic hydroperoxides that closely match those observed indoors. Unexpectedly, gas-phase
                    •
                    OH strongly suppressed VOC emissions. These results demonstrate that gas-phase radical-induced autoxidation governs SQ aging, challenging the prevailing ozone-centric view of indoor skin oil oxidation.

title: The network structure of the urban revolution
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Long-distance interaction has deep prehistoric roots, but the networks that emerged during the Urban Revolution were unprecedented in scale and organization. How early cities sustained this extensive connectivity in the absence of formal markets or centralized states remains a fundamental question. Focusing on the Uruk Expansion in Mesopotamia (ca. 3900 to 3000 BCE), we assemble the largest spatial dataset currently available and reconstruct transportation networks across three successive phases. Using network analysis, we show that an initially dendritic, river-based system evolved into modular regional clusters and ultimately into a more integrated structure linked by selective long-distance shortcuts. This transformation reduced dependence on key intermediaries and generated small world–like patterns combining strong local cohesion with efficient system-wide reach. These results demonstrate that decentralized interaction processes, supported in part by mobile intermediary communities, played a central role in sustaining early urban connectivity.

title: Highlights from an early base camp in Beringia 13,800 years ago: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the Late Pleistocene peopling of Alaska
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Human dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge (BLB) was a key event in the peopling of the Americas, but Beringia’s archaeological record remains poorly understood. In response, the Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ site in interior Alaska has been the focus of a multi-disciplinary study since 2016. The site contains three archaeological components dating to the Late Pleistocene, 13.8, 13, and 12.7 thousand years ago. The oldest component yielded an expressive array of cultural remains, including a unique hafted-biface form, osseous tools, diverse fauna, and well-preserved activity areas, a record unparalleled for this age in Beringia. Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ represents the earliest known Nenana Complex occupation east of the BLB, and its distinct hafted-biface form occurs in coeval sites west of the BLB, providing an important trans-Beringian cultural link. Although not Beringia’s oldest site, Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ reveals important information about Late Glacial peopling and settling-in behavior in this far northern setting.

title: SPRIZ (CCDC127) protein conserved in deuterostome animals is a rigid OMM–IMM tether that locally sets mitochondrial IMS volume
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The double-membrane nature of mitochondria generates an intermembrane volume through which ions, reactive oxygen species, and metabolites must flux to reach the matrix or cytosol, but whether this volume is a genetically specified structure remains unknown. We identify SPRIZ (spatial regulator of the intermembrane zone), the product of
                    Ccdc127
                    , a gene conserved across deuterostome animals. SPRIZ assembles into an ∼18-nanometer homodimeric tether anchored in the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) and inserted into the inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) through vertebrate-specific hydrophobic loops, physically spacing the two membranes and setting local intermembrane volume. Cryo-electron tomography of native mitochondria revealed rod-like densities spanning the intermembrane space (IMS), consistent with SPRIZ’s predicted rigid coiled-coil architecture and membrane-spanning topology. In mouse liver, two-dimensional morphometry measured ∼3-fold expansion of IMS area with SPRIZ and ∼5.5-fold with lengthened mitochondrial artificial increaser of the IMS (MARTINI); 3D electron tomography confirmed MARTINI’s greater OMM–IMM separation and normalized IMS volume. This expansion was functionally validated by increased
                    14
                    C-mannitol accessibility to the IMS and by impaired mitochondrial Ca
                    2+
                    uptake. Constitutive
                    Ccdc127/SPRIZ
                    knockout produced viable mice and, in liver mitochondria, preserved overall ultrastructure but caused modest IMS expansion, consistent with loss of local OMM–IMM constraints that stabilize membrane geometry at discrete sites. We therefore identify IMS volume as a genetically encoded and tunable architectural parameter of vertebrate mitochondria. In this model, SPRIZ is a molecular spacing system that locally sets OMM–IMM separation, shaping the environment through which metabolites, ions, and signals diffuse and establishing local gradients within the IMS.

title: Applications of a novel model-based real-time observer for electron density profile control experiments in TCV
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Real-time estimation and control of the electron plasma density profile is fundamental for monitoring and regulating particle confinement, fusion power, heating efficiency, exhaust performance, impurity concentration, and proximity to the density limit (Greenwald et alNucl. Fusion28 2199–207) in present and future tokamaks. This work presents the experimental applications of a multi-rate electron density observer (Pastore Fusion Eng. Des.192 113615) based on RAPDENS (Blanken Fusion Eng. Des.126 87–103), integrated into the TCV plasma control system, to control the density profile in a range of plasma scenarios relevant to future fusion power plants. Three main experimental contributions are reported. First, the observer enables control of the line-averaged electron density within the last-closed flux surface ( ) in ohmic, nitrogen-seeded plasmas with alternative divertor geometries, decoupling upstream density from scrape-off layer pickup in the interferometer signal—a limitation of the traditional control scheme. Second, local control of the central electron density below the ECH cutoff is demonstrated in L-mode plasmas with mixed ECH and neutral beam injection heating, where auxiliary-heating-induced profile peaking is treated as a disturbance to the control task. Real-time estimation and adjustment of the electron pinch velocity-to-diffusivity ratio improves the spatial accuracy of the profile reconstruction, especially in the core region. The underlying turbulent transport in this scenario is characterised via linear and non-linear gyrokinetic simulations with GENE, confirming quantitatively a TEM-dominated pumpout regime during ECH, which affects the amount of gas flux needed to sustain the target density reference. Last, simultaneous control of the edge-normalised density fraction and toroidal beta is demonstrated in high-performance H-mode plasmas ( , ), yielding reproducible scenarios with a device-agnostic density metric and robust handling of interferometer fringe jumps.

title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type–specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)–signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
source: Science
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

title: Thromboxane A2 receptor signalling amplifies osteoclastogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis through ACSL1 associated mitochondrial oxidative metabolism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Activated platelets contribute to inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis, but how platelet-derived signals promote bone erosion remains poorly understood. Here we show that thromboxane A2, a major mediator released by activated platelets, promotes the formation of bone-resorbing osteoclasts through the thromboxane A2 receptor. Markers of thromboxane A2 biosynthesis are increased in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, while pharmacological inhibition or genetic loss of its receptor suppresses osteoclastogenesis in mouse cells and mice. Integrated molecular analyses reveal that thromboxane A2 receptor signalling supports osteoclastogenesis by increasing fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-coenzyme A supply needed for mitochondrial energy metabolism, involving peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 beta, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma and acyl-coenzyme A synthetase long-chain family member 1. In male mice, receptor inhibition or genetic deletion reduces osteoclast accumulation and bone destruction. These findings identify thromboxane A2 signalling as a driver of inflammatory bone erosion and a potential therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis.

title: Microscale spatial fragmentation promotes bacterial survival under antibiotics
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Most bacteria inhabit fragmented microscale environments rather than well-mixed systems in which antibiotic efficacy is typically defined. Here, we show that microscale spatial fragmentation alone can deterministically promote bacterial survival under antibiotic exposure. A coarse-grained theoretical model predicts that, at fixed bulk cell density and antibiotic concentration, fragmentation generates refuges through two coupled mechanisms: slower growth, which reduces susceptibility to growth-dependent antibiotics, and a finite antibiotic-per-cell constraint that lowers the effective intracellular antibiotic concentration. Using a microdroplet platform spanning five orders of magnitude in volume, we experimentally confirm these predictions for β-lactams; we further demonstrate that the same fragmentation-mediated protection extends to antibiotics with distinct modes of action. Spatial fragmentation thus creates robust, non-genetic antibiotic refuges governed by physical constraints rather than resistance or collective protection, with implications for bacterial persistence in natural and clinical environments and for antibiotic design.

title: Genetic diversity and low-level infection of Malawi polyomavirus in pediatric patients in Brazil
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Malawi polyomavirus (MWPyV) has been detected in respiratory and gastrointestinal specimens, mostly in children; however there are limited data on its distribution and diversity. Here, we analyse n = 233 oropharyngeal swabs, collected from pediatric patients in São Paulo State, Brazil for MWPyV and potential co-infections using an integrated molecular, phylogenetic, and ultrastructural approach. We detect MWPyV DNA in 18 samples (7.7%) with low viral loads (mean 266 copies/reaction; range 13-2.3 × 103). Our phylogenetic analysis assigns six genomic sequences to genotype I and one to genotype III. The genome of genotype III shows evidence of putative recombination events with genomic regions related to genotypes II and III. One genotype I sequence forms a distinct phylogenetic branch, suggesting an unsampled or transitional lineage. Our findings provide evidence into the genomic diversity, viral recombination and potentially diverging lineages of MWPyV in pediatric patients.

title: Comparison of three pangolin coronaviruses showing distinct pathogenicity, transmissibility and potential for cross-species infection
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pangolins harbor SARS-CoV-2–related coronaviruses (PCoVs). We isolate three PCoVs (P8V, P11V, P5V) from confiscated Malayan pangolins and analyzed their genomes, evolution and functional properties. Phylogenetic analyses place these viruses in two clusters within the PCoV-GX lineage, revealing spike mutations that later convergently evolve in SARS-CoV-2. All viruses replicate efficiently in Vero E6 cells, with variable replication in human cell lines and organoids. In hACE2-transgenic mice, P11V and previously isolated P2V cause rapid, severe disease, whereas P8V and P5V exhibit delayed pathogenicity. Direct-contact transmission in hamsters is efficient for all strains, with lung pathology reflecting strain-specific virulence. These results demonstrate that PCoVs possess substantial infectivity, pathogenicity, and transmissibility, illustrating their adaptability, and highlight the role of pangolins as reservoirs of coronaviruses with zoonotic potential.

title: Brain-wide pathways for object identity and location are dominated by internal strategies
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: It is long thought that higher-order sensory processing is divided into two specialized cortical streams that encode in parallel either the identity of an object or its location (i.e., ‘what’ and ‘where’ streams). Here, using the mouse whisker system, we demonstrate an existence of two alternating brain-wide (beyond cortex) subnetworks that are primarily driven by internal strategies, rather than external parameters. We combine simultaneous brain-wide neuronal recordings in male mice trained to identify or locate a certain stimulus. We find that mice deploy either an active search or a passive sensation strategy during task performance. These strategies respectively drive two distinct brain-wide subnetworks, frontal and posterior related to an active and passive strategy respectively. Using a computational framework, we show that the posterior subnetwork encoded additional internal strategic parameters such as trial history, the first task of the day, and training history. When discarding the dominance of the frontal subnetwork, specific areas within the posterior subnetwork encoded meaningful task information regarding object identity and location. Integrated together, these two subnetworks may comprise optimal sensory integration.

title: Tissue composition shapes differential skeletal integration strategies during axolotl limb regeneration
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Limb regeneration requires rebuilding the missing structures and integrating them with stump tissues. Osteoclast-mediated tissue resorption is essential for skeletal integration during regeneration. However, it is unknown if skeletal tissue composition impacts its resorption and, if so, how it is regulated. Here, we show that osteoclast-mediated skeletal resorption is activated in amputations damaging the diaphysis, but not the epiphysis, of skeletal elements. We found that amputations in the calcified diaphysis trigger the sustained expression of RANKL and the chemokine Loc483, and that the latter is sufficient to induce osteoclast presence in non-resorbing amputations. Finally, our data suggests that the transcriptomic profile of the apical epithelial cap is impacted by the tissues injured by the amputation. Overall, our work reveals that tissue composition at the amputation plane shapes adaptations of the regenerative program, which ultimately contribute to the near-seamless tissue integration of the regenerating axolotl limb regardless of the amputation position.

title: A robust and accurate two-sample Mendelian randomization method with a large number of genetic variants
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Horizontal pleiotropy poses challenges in Mendelian randomization (MR) by biasing causal estimates, particularly when using numerous instrumental variables (IVs). We propose MRZ, a method that leverages IV-outcome association z-scores modeled as a mixture distribution to distinguish causal effects from IV-specific pleiotropy. MRZ classifies IVs into three categories: valid, uncorrelated pleiotropic, or correlated pleiotropic, enabling simultaneous estimation of causal and pleiotropic parameters through likelihood-based inference. Simulations demonstrate MRZ’s superior robustness and accuracy across diverse pleiotropic scenarios. When applied to investigate appendicular lean mass (ALM) and lipid traits, MRZ identifies significant negative causal effects of ALM on total cholesterol (TC) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), with no evidence of reverse causation. In contrast, existing methods frequently suggest bidirectional effects. Randomized controlled experiments in mice validate MRZ results, confirming ALM’s causal effects on TC/LDL-C but not vice versa. By addressing key limitations of conventional approaches vulnerable to horizontal pleiotropy, MRZ advances causal inference in complex trait architectures.

title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program.

title: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi. Six loci show evidence of association, including four related to homocysteine and folate metabolism - AHCYL1, PRICKLE2, GABBR2, and PLD2, with SNPs at the latter three also having direct effects on homocysteine-related metabolites in Mendelian Randomization. Collectively, one-carbon metabolism-related variants were significantly associated with edematous malnutrition (z = 3.2), with population differences linked to a shared East African genetic ancestry and distinct signatures of selection. These findings strengthen evidence implicating aberrant one-carbon metabolism in edematous malnutrition and highlight the utility of cell-free DNA, intra-continental admixture, and population genetics for mapping disease risk.

title: USP28 potentiates endothelial necroptosis via deubiquitinating NMMHC IIA in septic male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multi-organ injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. Mechanistically, USP28 stabilizes non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) by removing K48-linked ubiquitination at K1413. Moreover, NMMHC IIA promotes interferon-α/β receptor 1 (IFNAR1) trafficking to the plasma membrane, enhancing IFNAR1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) signaling and endothelial necroptosis. In turn, STAT1 transcriptionally increases USP28 expression, forming a positive feedback loop. Endothelial USP28 deletion or pharmacological inhibition attenuates sepsis-induced multi-organ injury, whereas USP28 overexpression exacerbates it. Conversely, endothelial NMMHC IIA or IFNAR1 overexpression largely abrogates the protection conferred by USP28 deficiency in septic male mice. These findings identify a USP28–NMMHC IIA axis that promotes endothelial necroptosis and multi-organ injury in sepsis through IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling.

title: Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pests pose escalating threats to forest ecosystem services globally, yet the patterns of forest vulnerability to these threats remain unclear. Leveraging over 7 million occurrence records of 1875 pest species, we identify northwestern Europe and eastern North America as global epicenters of forest-pest richness, dominated by insect fauna. Potential risk zones where timber production, carbon-rich forests, or diverse tree communities are exposed to high pest richness within and outside host native ranges cover 3.5% and 1.6% of forest globally, respectively. Forests in regions with stable temperatures, adequate precipitation, and high timber import volumes support high ecosystem services but also favor elevated pest richness, while forest fragmentation amplifies vulnerability to pests. Our findings provide a spatial blueprint for global pest management and underscore the urgent need for protecting forest health.

title: FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris, we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C. auris serial isolates from two critically unwell patients in London, UK. Population analysis profiling revealed echinocandin heteroresistance, and in vitro culture of clinical isolates at supra-MIC concentrations of anidulafungin (8 μg/ml) exhibited morphotypic heterogeneity. Small colony variants (SCVs) and large colony variants (LCVs) showed elevated MICs with polyploidy (to 4n and above) alongside adaptive changes in cell wall β−1,3-glucan content. LCVs contained significantly more mutations in calcineurin-related stress tolerance pathway gene CRZ1 compared to clinical parents and SCVs, associated with further increases in MIC. These findings indicate progressive step-wise accrual of adaptation to echinocandins, including genomic instability, alterations in stress tolerance pathways, and cell wall remodelling, paving the way for resistance emergence.

title: RNF130 ameliorates renal injury and inflammation by inhibiting macrophage pyroptosis through ubiquitination degradation of PDCD4 in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Macrophage pyroptosis has been identified as a contributor to acute kidney injury (AKI), but the underlying mechanisms involved remain unclear. Herein, we identify that ring finger protein 130 (RNF130) RNF130 is significantly downregulated in both mice and patients with AKI. Myeloid cell-specific loss of RNF130 aggravates renal pathological damage and facilitates macrophage pyroptosis in AKI mouse models. Proteomics analyses and experimental validation show that RNF130 deficiency prevents the ubiquitination of programmed cell death 4 (PDCD4) dependent on the lysine 402 of PDCD4. Activated PDCD4 promotes the phosphorylation of NF-κB and STAT3, triggering NLRP3 inflammasome activation and caspase-1-mediated cleavage of GSDMD, contributing to macrophage pyroptosis. Overexpression of PDCD4 nullifies the beneficial role of RNF130. High-throughput screening of a compound library identified that Nystose effectively mitigated renal injury in ischemic AKI mice by targeting and upregulating RNF130. These findings highlight the potential of RNF130 as a promising target for AKI.

title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Potential health risk associated with dietary intake of nanoplastics has emerged as a global health concern, yet approaches for reducing gastrointestinal nanoplastic exposure remain poorly explored. Here, we investigated whether increasing dietary fiber intake influences the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics in male mice utilizing a visible/near-infrared dual fluorescence labeling technique combined with non-invasive imaging. The estimated retention rates of nanoplastics-associated fluorescence are decreased by two and seven times in male mice fed with medium fiber diet and high fiber diet compared to those with standard fiber diet, 24 h after oral intake. High fiber diet is associated with attenuated nanoplastics-induced epithelial damage to intestinal tract and declined detectable NIR fluorescence in important organs such as liver during 28-d oral exposure to nanoplastics. In vitro simulations show that dietary fiber physically encapsulates and adheres nanoplastics to decrease their bioavailability. Understanding how dietary constituents influence the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics may provide a scientific basis for the future development of dietary strategies aimed at reducing nanoplastic exposure.

title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

title: Uhrf1 loss disrupts CTCF-associated chromatin organization during early mouse embryogenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: UHRF1 is a chromatin-binding protein essential for maintaining DNA methylation and histone modification states, yet its integrated role in vivo remains incompletely understood. To define its function, we generated conditional Uhrf1 knockout embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and embryos. Uhrf1⁻/⁻ ESCs exhibited near-complete loss of 5mC and 5hmC but maintained pluripotency, whereas Uhrf1-null embryos developed normally until E8.5 and then failed to develop further by E9.5, phenocopying Dnmt1 loss. Single-cell multi-omic (ME-seq) profiling of E8.5 embryos revealed impaired lineage stabilization, widespread hypomethylation, and disrupted chromatin architecture. Uhrf1 loss was associated with altered CTCF-associated chromatin signal, broad remodeling of chromatin contacts, altered cis-regulatory relationships, and reduced predicted BMP-related ligand–receptor communication, particularly within neural crest populations. These findings identify Uhrf1 as a central regulator that tightly couples DNA methylation maintenance to 3D genome organization during gastrulation, thereby, directing early lineage specification and positioning Uhrf1 as a pivotal mediator of epigenetic information transfer during early embryogenesis.

title: Regulation of target gene expression by chromatin-associated protein-coding transcripts in plants
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. Genome-wide profiling of RNA–chromatin interactions in Arabidopsis has uncovered widespread associations between protein-coding transcripts and distinct genomic loci, implying that they possess regulatory functions. Here, we found that BT2 and GSL8 transcripts modulate target gene transcription independently of their protein products through distinct mechanisms. The BT2 transcript represses transcription of its targets CEP2 and MRF4 by forming RNA–DNA triplexes, thereby restricting root growth and promoting flowering, whereas GSL8 acts through a triplex-independent pathway. Our findings unveil intrinsic regulatory activities of protein-coding transcripts, challenging the canonical definition of mRNA function and blurring the functional distinction between coding and noncoding RNAs in the context of genome evolution.

title: Boundary Guided Liquid‐Bridge Adhesion for Robotic Pick‐and‐Release
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐bridge‐mediated adhesion provides conformal contact with rough surfaces and gentle interaction with fragile microstructures, making it attractive for object manipulation. However, controlling liquid‐bridge formation and retraction under non‐ideal interfacial conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a switchable liquid‐bridge adhesion strategy using a two‐tiered stamp with spatially patterned wettability. Boundary‐guided pinning confines liquid spreading to form a stable bridge for pickup and guides liquid retraction toward bridge breakup for controlled release. This design converts liquid‐bridge adhesion from an uncontrolled capillary phenomenon into a controllable interfacial mechanism. The strategy enables preload‐free adhesion switching, tunable adhesion forces, robust manipulation across surfaces with diverse roughness and wettability, and damage‐free contact with fragile microstructures. Integrated with a robotic platform, the stamp functions as a liquid‐bridge‐based robotic end effector for pick‐and‐place manipulation and robotic placement, providing a route toward ultra‐gentle manufacturing and microelectronic assembly.

title: Stereoselective polysubstituted bicyclo[1.1.0]butane synthesis by rhodium-catalyzed kinetic resolution
source: Science
abstract: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) are a distinctive class of strained small-ring carbocycles of growing importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. However, the enantioselective synthesis of polysubstituted BCBs remains a largely unsolved challenge. In this study, we report a general chemical platform for the stereoselective assembly of chiral or meso 1,2,3,4-tetrasubstituted BCBs from internal alkynes and carbenes through stepwise [2+1+1’] or one-pot [2+1+1] cycloaddition reactions, respectively. Successful execution of these transformations exploits the combination of triftosylhydrazones (carbene precursors) and chiral dirhodium catalysts. The sterically hindered catalyst Rh 2 ( R -3,5- di PheTPCP) 4 features a confined chiral microenvironment that enables exquisite discrimination between cyclopropene enantiomers, affording highly enantioenriched polysubstituted BCBs through kinetic resolution upon reaction with chiral rhodium carbenes. This chemistry operates under mild reaction conditions, uses readily available starting materials, and exhibits broad substrate scope.

title: Human-enhanced tsunami hazard in large lakes
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Worldwide, human-induced erosion enhances sediment delivery to lake deltas, increasing their susceptibility to collapse. In Lake Iseo, northern Italy, two millennia of intensified land use tripled sediment flux, oversteepening the delta and preconditioning it for failure. Here we show from geological records and numerical simulations that earthquakes in 1117 CE (Mw 6.5) and 1222 CE (Mw 6.0) triggered major subaqueous delta collapses, generating massive tsunamis with maximum run-ups of ~50 m and ~13 m, respectively. Historical accounts from the Vatican Library and archeological evidence support these reconstructions. Since the last collapse, eight centuries of human-induced erosion have rebuilt the delta, leaving shoreline populations highly vulnerable to future earthquake-triggered failures. A global lake synthesis showed that human-driven erosion has reached its highest levels since the Industrial Era, progressively overloading deltas worldwide; thus, similar catastrophic failures may become more likely in the future. These findings reveal a persistent, human-amplified mechanism of lacustrine tsunami generation and intensity with major implications for hazard assessment.

title: Modular van der Waals MOSFETs through layer-by-layer chalcogen substitutions
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the local electrostatic field of the chalcogen p -orbitals dictates the crystal field splitting of the transition metal d -orbitals, stabilizing diverse electronic states from semiconducting and semimetallic to exotic topological phases. On-demand substitution of the lattice chalcogens is therefore an efficient route to tuning TMDC electronic phases. Here, we custom-molded van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by layer-by-layer vapor-phase chalcogen substitution starting from p -type WSe 2 multilayers into which we locally inscribed insulating WO x , n -type WS 2 , and semimetallic WTe 2 . This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WO x /WSe 2 local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide–semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.

title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

title: Gate-tunable chiral spin mode in WSe 2 /WS 2 moiré superlattices
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: The interplay between many-body and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effects can lead to previously unobserved phenomena in solids. Chiral spin modes (CSMs) are collective spin excitations that arise from such interplay and connect states with opposite chirality. Here, we report a gate-tunable CSM that occurs between conduction SOC-split minibands in near-0°-twisted WSe 2 /WS 2 bilayers. This mode manifests as a sharp resonance with giant Raman efficiency in the pseudovector-symmetry channel of the Raman spectra. By varying the filling, the CSM transitions from a chiral spin exciton to an excitonic polaron. The spin-flip nature is directly confirmed by the Zeeman effect, and the filling dependence indicates a charge-transfer insulator at unity filling. Our results demonstrate that transition metal–dichalcogenide moiré superlattices are a fertile platform for exploring exotic low-lying collective excitations.
